Limitation 
It is important to acknowledge that while this 
study aims to investigate the potential 
performance of green infrastructure (GI) 
features in reducing runoff in urban land use, 
it is subject to a primary limitation. The 
runoff coefficient values (C and C′) and 
rainfall intensity (i) are derived from the 
literature, introducing uncertainty in the 
absolute accuracy of the results. However, 
the primary focus of this study remains on 
comparing the relative potential of various GI 
features for runoff reduction rather than on 
providing 
highly 
precise 
quantitative 
estimates. To enhance accuracy in future 
hydrological studies, the runoff coefficient 
(C) for given drainage areas should be 
examined. These values are primarily 
contingent on three critical factors: soil 
properties, 
land 
use 
types, 
and 
the 
catchment's slope, which influence flow 
characteristics. Furthermore, the runoff 
coefficient of green infrastructure features 
(C′), their specific layer criteria, soil 
composition, 
vegetation, 
and 
the 
geographical attributes of their respective 
catchments should be further considered.

Abstract 
As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly impacts all facets of human life—from healthcare and 
finance to education and surveillance—conversations surrounding AI ethics have gained 
prominence. However, most ethical debates concerning AI are rooted in Western intellectual 
traditions. This study advocates for the incorporation of Buddhist ethics and Eastern moral 
traditions, including the Madhyamaka philosophy of Nagarjuna, as crucial components in 
redefining the future of AI. Buddhism, emphasizing compassion, interdependence, non-
harming, and emptiness (sūnyatā) (សុញ្ញតា) presents a moral framework wherein technical 
advancement serves as a method to alleviate suffering (Dukkha Samudaya) (ទុក្ខសមុទយៈ) rather 
than an ultimate goal. The study presents a “Humane AI” framework by connecting the 
Buddhist perspective with the intrinsic constraints of AI, such as its lack of subjectivity and 
inability to achieve wisdom. This framework prioritizes mindfulness, intention, and alleviation 
of suffering, encouraging developers and policymakers to walk a Middle Path (មជ្ឈិមាបដិបទា) 
in AI development. 
Keywords: Humane AI, Eastern Moral Philosophy, Emptiness (Śūnyatā), Compassionate AI, Middle Way 
(Madhyamaka)

2. Suffering (dukkha) in the Age of AI 
2.1. Suffering 
There are several ways that AI makes 
Dukkha, or suffering, getting worse, both 
directly and indirectly. The aforementioned 
are some of the methods: 
• Emotional Suffering (citta dukkha) 
(ចិត្តទុក្ខៈ): 
Algorithms that change 
how people pay attention (like on 
social media) can make people 
depressed, anxious, lonely, and hurt 
themselves. 
• Inequality: AI-powered systems can 
make healthcare, education, jobs, and 
law enforcement even more unequal. 
• Surveillance and Control: Facial 
recognition and data collection can 
take away your freedom and privacy. 
• Automation Anxiety: Millions of 
people are worried about losing their 
jobs because of automation, which 
makes them unsure about their future 
and their finances. 
AI could help minimize suffering in some 
ways, including by improving medical 
diagnosis, 
predicting 
disasters, 
and 
personalizing 
learning. 
However, 
the 
existing 
paradigms 
that 
guide 
its 
development typically don't include ethical 
reflection based on a deep, caring 
relationship with all living things.

Applying Nagarjuna’s insights on the 
middle path of emptiness, AI ethics can be 
reframed as the following: 
● There is “No Inherent Evil or Good 
in AI”: Technology is empty—it is not 
inherently good or evil. Its ethical 
value arises from context and intention. 
● On Interdependence: AI systems are 
embedded in vast networks—data 
collectors, 
programmers, 
users, 
environments. Ethical responsibility is 
distributed and relational. 
● On the Middle  Path: Avoid both 
extremes of AI utopianism and AI 
fatalism. Ethical assessment must 
navigate between extremes. 
Madhyamaka as a major philosophical 
tradition challenges developers and ethicists 
to abandon egoistic, individualistic frames 
of control and instead cultivate an awareness 
of systems, conditions, and dependent 
responsibilities. 
3. Humanistic Buddhism and AI Practice  
3.1. Core Ethical Values for AI 
In accordance with Buddhist teachings, we 
present the subsequent ethical framework 
for Humane AI (Table 1). An ethical 
approach to AI, informed by fundamental 
Buddhist 
principles, 
commences 
with 
Ahimsa, the dedication to prevent harm, 
guaranteeing that technology enhances 
rather than detracts. It is influenced by 
Karunā, 
integrating 
compassion 
into 
algorithms to ensure they operate with 
empathy and consideration. Through Sati, 
developers engage in conscious awareness 
when 
managing 
data—ensuring 
transparency, ethics, and respect. Utilizing 
Upaya, AI systems employ contextual 
understanding to adeptly address various 
human demands. Rooted in Anattā, the 
doctrine of non-self, AI is engineered not 
solely for ego or profit, but for the common 
welfare of humanity. These principles serve 
as a framework for developers, politicians, 
and educators to assess and direct AI 
initiatives.

Both humanistic Buddhism and post-
humanist ethics concern the hierarchical 
boundaries that separate life and death, 
people and machines. The idea of oneness 
and coexistence that Master Hsing Yun talks 
about is similar to post-humanist ideas of 
transcendence and pluralism. However 
Humanistic Buddhism says that people must 
change from the inside out. Zheng (2024) 
discovers that robust AI and transhumanism 
may prioritize physical enhancement over 
spiritual enlightenment. 
Nagarjuna's perspective on non-duality 
contests the subject-object dualism. AI 
systems are intrinsically linked to human 
intention, data, and interaction. 
This encompasses the subsequent elements: 
• Collective Accountability: We jointly 
shape the advantages and detriments of 
AI. 
• Shared Existence: AI is not an isolated 
entity but rather an integral component 
of an interdependent moral ecosystem. 
• Analyzing Selfish Design: Transition 
from control-oriented frameworks to 
care-oriented frameworks. 
Nagarjuna instructs us to perceive AI as 
devoid 
of 
intrinsic 
value—neither 
intrinsically beneficial nor detrimental, but 
potent contingent upon its causes and 
conditions. This perspective enables us to 
uphold ethical vigilance while fostering 
creative openness.

4. Conclusion 
AI transcends mere functionality; it is a 
moral artifact shaped by the developers' 
objectives and worldview. Buddhist ethics, 
particularly 
Nagarjuna's 
philosophy, 
provide a comprehensive, compassionate, 
and 
interdependent 
framework 
for 
contemplating 
and 
directing 
the 
advancement of AI. Confucianism posits 
that the cultivation of virtue, social harmony 
(he), and humaneness (ren) necessitates that 
AI facilitate moral interactions and foster a 
society grounded in kindness and propriety. 
Similarly, 
Aristotle’s 
virtue 
ethics 
emphasizes phronesis (practical wisdom) 
and the shaping of moral character through 
habituated action—paralleling the Buddhist 
emphasis on intention (cetana) and ethical 
mindfulness. By embracing values such as 
non-harming, compassion, mindfulness, and 
skillful means, we can reframe AI not as a 
vehicle of domination or alienation, but as a 
partner in the alleviation of suffering and the 
cultivation of well-being. A Humane AI is 
not merely more accurate, more intelligent, 
or more productive. It is more aware, more 
compassionate, and more humble. It is 
grounded in the ancient question: “Does this 
help reduce suffering?” If the answer is yes, 
then we are not just building better machines. 
We are becoming better human beings.

Aristotle’s 
virtue 
ethics 
emphasizes phronesis (practical wisdom) 
and the shaping of moral character through 
habituated action—paralleling the Buddhist 
emphasis on intention (cetana) and ethical 
mindfulness. By embracing values such as 
non-harming, compassion, mindfulness, and 
skillful means, we can reframe AI not as a 
vehicle of domination or alienation, but as a 
partner in the alleviation of suffering and the 
cultivation of well-being. A Humane AI is 
not merely more accurate, more intelligent, 
or more productive. It is more aware, more 
compassionate, and more humble. It is 
grounded in the ancient question: “Does this 
help reduce suffering?” If the answer is yes, 
then we are not just building better machines. 
We are becoming better human beings.

the Policy and Strategy on ICT in Education 2018, and ICT Masterplan 2020, to drive excellence and 
innovation in education, particularly in secondary schools, as outlined in the Cambodia Education 2030 
Roadmap for Sustainable Development Goal 4.

trainers will guide participants through the seamless integration of emerging innovative pedagogies and

learning experiences to interactive digital resources, participants will explore a diverse range of transformative 
pedagogies and technology integration tailored to meet the unique needs of today's learners.

• 
Master a diverse range of pedagogical techniques and technology integration methods to enhance 
student engagement and academic performance.

Develop the capacity to critically analyse and evaluate the impact of technology on teaching practices, 
allowing for informed decision-making and adaptation.

4. Course Outlines 
4.1. Innovative Teaching Methods (45 hours = 3 credits): This course explores cutting-edge pedagogies, 
learn how to create engaging lessons, and develop strategies for diverse learners. By the end of this course, you 
will be able to: 
• 
Innovate Your Teaching: Explore the role of teachers in the 21st century and introductory principles 
of innovative teaching methods. 
• 
Design Engaging Lessons: Build upon your understanding of innovative teaching by learning 
instructional design principles for effective learning and classroom management. 
• 
Integrate Technology: Discover how to effectively incorporate technology into your teaching 
practices, using learning theories and diverse learner strategies to enhance your instruction. 
• 
Evaluate Student Progress: Apply your knowledge by understanding how to assess and evaluate student 
learning, including incorporating technology into your assessment methods to measure progress. 
• 
Create a Mastery Project: Demonstrate your mastery of innovative teaching by creating a final project that 
showcases your skills and knowledge, incorporating all that you've learned throughout the course. 
4.2. Technology-Assisted Teaching Methods (45 hours = 3 credits): This course discovers how to integrate 
technology into your teaching practice, learn about LMS and learning management, and develop multimedia 
presentations. By the end of this course, you will be able to: 
• 
Integrate Technology Effectively: Learn how to effectively integrate technology into your teaching 
practice, from introductory principles to hands-on application. 
• 
Master Learning Management Systems: Understand how to use learning management systems and 
develop strategies for managing digital content and resources. 
• 
Design a Digital Classroom: Discover the role of technology in education, including instructional 
strategies, diverse learning styles, and educational tech applications. 
• 
Create Multimedia Presentations: Develop engaging multimedia presentations, digital content, and 
learn about the use of video, AR, and VR in the classroom. 
• 
Teach in the Digital Age: Apply your knowledge by creating a final presentation that showcases your 
ability to effectively integrate technology into your teaching practice.

Preface 
This fourth volume of Selected Works: Contemporary Perspectives on Cambodia 
and the Asia Pacific continues the reflections presented in Volumes I, II, and III. It emerges 
at a defining moment in Cambodia’s long journey toward state modernization—one shaped by 
sustained political stability, propelled by institutional and economic reform, and challenged by 
profound changes in the regional and global environment. As Cambodia enters a new era of 
leadership, economic aspiration, and diplomatic engagement, the essays collected here offer 
both a chronicle of recent national developments and a forward-looking assessment of the 
opportunities and uncertainties that lie ahead. 
Published in Khmer Times and other platforms between November 2023 and December 
2024, the articles capture the evolution of events during a period of notable transformation. 
Domestically, Cambodia experienced a peaceful transfer of power unparalleled in its modern 
political history. Regionally, the Asia Pacific confronted intensifying geopolitical rivalry, growing 
economic fragility, and shifting diplomatic alignments amid global power reconfigurations. 
Globally, post-pandemic recovery, the climate crisis, and rapid technological disruptions 
demanded that small and middle states adapt with agility and foresight. 
Against this backdrop, the writings in this volume seek to contextualize Cambodia’s 
trajectory within broader regional and international dynamics. They reflect my enduring belief 
that Cambodia must continue to shape its future through transformative leadership, 
accountable and agile governance, people-centered development, and proactive engagement 
in regional and global affairs. 
Cambodia’s Transformation and Peace 
A central theme throughout Part I is the indispensable foundation of peace. Cambodia’s 
hard-won stability, achieved after decades of conflict, continues to form the bedrock of national 
development and strategic choice. Peace enabled the revival of political institutions, the 
expansion of democratic participation, and the steady modernization of the economy. As the 
country moves forward, peace remains not an endpoint but an ever-relevant condition that 
must be nurtured, protected, and renewed. 
This volume underscores how Cambodia’s new generation of leaders—embodied most 
notably by Prime Minister Hun Manet—inherits both the achievements and the unfinished 
tasks of the past three decades. Their mandate is to preserve national unity while accelerating 
reforms in governance, human capital development, economic diversification, innovation, and 
international integration.

Leadership Transition and Institutional Renewal 
Several essays examine the leadership philosophy and political outlook of Prime 
Minister Hun Manet. Rooted in the historical legacy of the Cambodian People’s Party yet 
representing a generational shift, Hun Manet brings a leadership style informed by 
international education, technological awareness, reform-mindedness, and a commitment to 
expanding engagement both domestically and globally. 
His rise reflects a broader renewal of Cambodia’s political and technocratic class. A 
new cohort of ministers, advisors, and institutional leaders has emerged, emphasizing 
professionalism, accountability, performance-based governance, and strengthened state 
capacity. This renewal is essential for tackling corruption, enhancing public service delivery, 
and building the resilient institutions needed for Cambodia to realize its aspiration of becoming 
a high-income country by 2050. 
Economic Modernization in an Era of Global Uncertainty 
The section on Cambodia’s economy highlights the urgency of accelerating reform in a 
global landscape marked by uncertainty—whether due to disrupted supply chains, 
technological competition, shifting investment patterns, or climate-related pressures. 
Cambodia must move beyond labor-intensive manufacturing and build an economy anchored 
in innovation, skills, green transformation, and economic resilience. 
These essays examine how domestic governance reforms intersect with external 
economic opportunities, particularly in the areas of economic diplomacy, SME revitalization, 
financial stability, and industrial diversification. At the heart of this transformation is a strategic 
investment in human capital: strengthening education, nurturing technical and digital skills, 
and empowering Cambodia’s youth to contribute to national development. 
Equally significant is the role of major infrastructure initiatives such as the Funan Techo 
Canal. This landmark project symbolizes Cambodia’s ambition to become a logistics and 
economic gateway for the Mekong subregion, enabling greater connectivity, competitiveness, 
and economic sovereignty. It demonstrates the country’s long-term commitment to shaping its 
own development trajectory with confidence and strategic purpose. 
Diplomacy, Sovereignty, and the Art of Navigation 
Part II broadens the analysis to Cambodia’s engagement with the region and the world. 
Cambodia’s foreign policy—anchored in independence, multilateralism, and respect for 
international law—must navigate an increasingly complex geopolitical environment dominated 
by great-power rivalry, especially between China and the United States. 
The essays illustrate that Cambodia’s strategic posture is not defined by passive 
alignment but by pragmatic calculation. Cambodia seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, diversify 
partnerships, strengthen ASEAN centrality, and champion cooperation on shared transnational 
challenges. Discussions on the South China Sea, ASEAN dynamics, and Cambodia’s relations 
with China, the United States, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and Thailand demonstrate how small 
and middle states can exercise meaningful agency even amid asymmetric power relations. 
Cambodia’s diplomacy strives to avoid enmity, foster trust, and serve as a bridge for dialogue. 
Humanitarianism, Society, and the Spirit of Shared Prosperity 
Beyond geopolitics, the volume also engages the human dimension of Cambodia’s 
national transformation. Essays on the Cambodian Red Cross, youth empowerment, social 
innovation, public health, and the evolving Cambodian dream remind us that national progress 
is measured not only by economic metrics but by the well-being of communities and the 
strength of social solidarity. 
Humanitarian innovation emerges as a vital pillar—mobilizing community-based 
responses, empowering young people, and fostering partnerships that link local capacities 
with international networks. These reflections highlight the moral and societal foundations of 
sustainable development and inclusive prosperity. 
Closing Reflection 
Although written in response to specific moments and issues, the articles in this volume 
aim to serve as building blocks for broader conversations on Cambodia’s strategic direction. 
They embody a commitment to balanced analysis, constructive reflection, and an unwavering 
belief in the potential of the Cambodian nation. 
Cambodia today stands at a crossroads—facing global headwinds yet rich in 
opportunity. The country must navigate geopolitical turbulence, enhance democratic and 
institutional resilience, modernize its governance systems, and unleash the creativity and 
capabilities of its people. 
If Cambodia’s recent history teaches anything, it is that the nation possesses 
extraordinary resilience. From the ruins of conflict, Cambodia has risen with determination, 
vision, and dignity. The journey continues—shaped by hard-earned lessons, sustained by 
collective aspirations, and strengthened by the courage of its people. 
It is my hope that this volume contributes, in a modest but meaningful way, to ongoing 
efforts to understand, reflect upon, and shape Cambodia’s future within the Asia Pacific and 
the wider world.

Hun Manet, the hope of Cambodia 

Over the last 500 years, Cambodia has seen various waves of violent transitions 
of power. Thanks to the win-win policy spearheaded by Prime Minister Hun Sen, 
Cambodia had achieved peace in late 1998, after all Khmer factions came together 
under one roof, one constitution, and one government. 
Peace should not be taken granted. We need to keep nurturing and building the 
foundations of peace, especially amidst rising geopolitical uncertainties and volatilities. 
Political leaders are held accountable for national unity, peace, and development. 
Prime Minister Hun Sen has never abandoned Cambodians. He remains loyal to 
his people in all circumstances and events. This is his leadership trait. As a historical 
power transition is going to take place after the general election in July this year, he 
needs to ensure that the transition will go peacefully and smoothly. He has shown zero 
tolerance towards those who aim to destroy our hard-earned peace. 
If our next leader is not carefully chosen, it would leave opportunities for foreign 
forces to interfere with our internal affairs most likely through the oppositions or it could 
mean anarchy within the Cambodian People’s Party (CPP). If there is no party unity, the 
civil servants would be too preoccupied to deal with party politics and won’t be able to 
serve the Cambodian people as they were voted in to do. 
We have already seen the example of how a scenario like this would play out with 
British politics. For the last few years, there is no party unity or solidarity within the 
reigning Conservative Party. The different factions within the party have been so 
preoccupied with competing for leadership that has left the British people facing high 
inflation, food insecurity, energy, and health care crisis. 
Consequently, as emphasised before, it is crucial that the next leader of a political 
party is carefully chosen in order for the country to remain peaceful and stable. As such, 
this is a crucial task for the Prime Minister to choose who to pass the torch to, in order to 
lead our country into the next era of peace, stability and prosperity. 
At the 2021 party congress, CPP’s Central Committee unanimously voted to 
anoint Mr Hun Manet as its future Prime Minister candidate. Mr Manet is the most 
qualified and decorated candidate to be our next prime minister. Here are some facts. He 
is the first ever Cambodian to have graduated from the prestigious United States Military

West Point Academy in 1999, he then obtained his Master of Arts in Economics from 
New York University in 2002 and a PhD in Economics of the University of Bristol in 2008. 
After his academic journey, he joined and led the Ministry of Defence’s National 
Counter-Terrorism Special Forces where he worked his way up the military ladder to be 
appointed as the Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces 
and the Commander of the Royal Cambodian Army. He came into national and 
international spotlight when he took a leadership role in overseeing the negotiations 
during the 2008-2011 Cambodian-Thailand border conflict. 
Apart from the military duties, he has been actively involved in philanthropic social 
works.  As the Chief of the Samdech Techo Hun Sen Scholarship Committee and the 
Samdech Techo Scholarship Association, he provides scholarship opportunities to 
thousands of Cambodian youths to enrol in universities across Cambodia. 
Along with his wife Pich Chanmony, he founded and serve as chairman of the 
Board of Directors of the Samdech Techo Youth Volunteer Doctor Association, which 
mobilises thousands of medical professionals, trainees, and volunteers to provide free 
healthcare in rural areas throughout Cambodia. Most remarkably, during the COVID-19 
pandemic, he spearheaded the projects to lead medical teams to fight against the 
disease and established treatment facilities across Phnom Penh in order to provide 
accessible healthcare for the Cambodian people, which resulted in a great success.  
This of course contributed to the overall effort of our country’s fight against the pandemic. 
In regard to the CPP responsibilities, he was nominated as head of the CPP’s 
youth wing in 2020, where membership has been enlarged and diversified since this new 
leadership came into effect. He understands that, as a leader, he needs support from all 
of CPP’s diverse pool of members and not just the political elites. With this in mind, his 
most noticeable reformative strategy for CPP was to increase engagements with 
Cambodian diaspora communities overseas, which over the years has become a playing 
field for the oppositions to monopolise their influence and propagandas, in which they 
were succeeding. Not only that these communities still have families in Cambodia, 
crucially, they also play a role in how external actors perceive Cambodia as a whole. 
Oppositions has been able to spread their propaganda to other governments 
through the Cambodian diasporas with narratives of Cambodia being embroiled with 
corruption, communism, nepotism, and Vietnamese/Chinese puppets.

Mr Manet understands that in order to rectify these narratives, CPP needs to 
provide a safe platform where they can engage with the Cambodian diasporas so that 
they would feel valued. At the same time, these Cambodian diasporas abroad can also 
be kept informed of developments in Cambodia in order to see how far we have 
developed and prospered since the days of Khmer Rouge. 
Furthermore, he understands that engagements with CPP youths is crucial for the 
future of Cambodia as well since the youths will be leading our country one day. It is 
important that they are valued by CPP and that they will be more political involved in 
attributing to relevant up-to-date policymaking one day. 
With this vision in mind along with his down-to-earth, approachable and caring 
personal characteristics, he is beloved by CPP especially by his youth wing, which is 
crucial to having a peaceful transition of power in the future. 
With these credentials, how could one say that Mr  Manet is not a qualified prime 
ministerial candidate? The critics should not be so laser focused on the fact that he is the 
son of Prime Minister Hun Sen but that he is a young Cambodian leader who has earned 
merits and trust from the people. He has millions of supporters behind him. 
In terms of foreign policy, it is widely believed that Mr  Manet will continue to follow 
an independent foreign policy based on international law and core national interests. 
Pragmatism and hedging strategy will continue to inform the next generation of 
Cambodian foreign policy makers. Cambodia’s vision as a global peace maker will gain 
new momentum.

The Interconnectedness among Peace, Democracy,

Cambodia has experienced a tumultuous history marred by conflicts and unrest, 
which has instilled in the nation a profound appreciation for the importance of peace. 
Through firsthand experiences, Cambodia has witnessed the devastating consequences 
of violence and instability on its people and the nation as a whole. 
Consequently, Cambodia recognizes that sustainable development and the well-
being of its citizens can only be achieved within a peaceful environment. This editorial 
explores the interconnectedness among peace, democracy, good governance, and 
development from a Cambodian perspective, emphasizing their mutually reinforcing 
nature. 
 Peace as the Foundation 
In Cambodia, peace is considered a paramount priority due to its historical 
context. The nation acknowledges that peace serves as the bedrock upon which 
democracy, good governance, and development can flourish. 
Cambodia’s commitment to peace is rooted in its understanding that without a 
peaceful environment, sustainable development and the well-being of its citizens cannot 
be realized. The experiences of violence and instability have shaped Cambodia’s 
dedication to fostering peace, as it has witnessed the positive impact that peace has on 
societal progress. 
 Democracy as a Catalyst 
Cambodia recognizes the significance of democracy in ensuring peace and 
stability. The core principles of inclusivity, transparency, and accountability inherent in 
democracy play a vital role in fostering dialogue, protecting human rights, and fostering 
social cohesion. 
By upholding democratic values, Cambodia empowers its citizens, providing them

Political Parties and Democracy in Cambodia 

Cambodia, having emerged from the shadow of the Khmer Rouge regime, has 
undergone significant transformations in its political landscape. 
A key driving force behind its democratic development has been the establishment 
of a multi-party system. This op-ed aims to highlight the vital role political parties play in 
fostering democracy, while acknowledging both the progress made and the challenges 
that remain in Cambodia’s journey towards an inclusive and vibrant multi-party system. 
Since the reintroduction of multiparty politics in the 1990s, Cambodia has witnessed 
the growth of various political parties, each representing different ideologies, interests, and 
constituencies. This multiplicity of parties has allowed for diverse political perspectives, 
enabling citizens to exercise their democratic rights by choosing representatives who align 
with their values and aspirations. 
The multi-party system has also facilitated a competitive political environment, 
encouraging parties to engage in robust debates, policy discussions, and electoral 
campaigns. This competition serves as a check on power, pushing political actors to 
respond to the needs and concerns of the electorate. Furthermore, multiple parties provide 
citizens with meaningful choices during elections, ensuring that their voices are heard, and 
their preferences are represented. 
Cambodia’s democratic progress has been a subject of global attention. The 
Kingdom has made notable strides over the past two decades, with political parties 
emerging as vital pillars of a functioning democracy. 
Political parties are the lifeblood of any democratic society, providing a platform for 
diverse voices and opinions. In Cambodia, they play a crucial role in representing the 
interests, aspirations, and concerns of citizens across the nation. By fielding candidates 
for elections and engaging in political discourse, parties ensure that a multitude of 
perspectives are presented to the electorate, fostering a pluralistic and inclusive 
democracy. 
Effective political parties serve as vehicles for citizen engagement and political 
education. They mobilize and organize individuals, giving them an opportunity to 
participate actively in the political process. Through party membership, citizens can 
contribute to policy formulation, advocate for their communities, and actively shape the 
future of their nation. Political parties act as platforms for debate, encouraging informed 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 8 
Volume IV 
discussions and raising awareness about critical issues, thereby strengthening democratic 
values among citizens. 
One of the primary functions of political parties in Cambodia’s democracy is to hold 
those in power accountable. Different parties play a critical role in providing checks and 
balances, ensuring that the ruling party operates within the framework of the law and 
respects democratic principles. By scrutinizing government actions, proposing alternative 
policies, and advocating for transparency and good governance, political parties contribute 
to the overall accountability of the political system. 
Political parties also play a crucial role in policy formulation and national 
development. Through their political platforms and manifestos, parties articulate their 
visions for the country’s future and propose solutions to societal challenges. By engaging 
in rigorous policy debates, parties contribute to the development of well-informed and 
robust policies. Furthermore, successful parties often serve as incubators of political talent, 
nurturing individuals who can lead the nation and shape its future trajectory. 
While political parties play essential roles in Cambodia’s democracy, there are 
challenges that need to be addressed. It is crucial to foster an environment where parties 
can operate freely and without undue interference. Ensuring a level playing field during 
elections, protecting freedom of speech and assembly, and promoting transparent 
campaign financing are all essential elements for a vibrant party system. 
Parties must strive to be representative of the diverse population of Cambodia, 
including women, youth, and marginalized communities. By promoting inclusivity and 
diversity within their ranks, parties can better address the needs of the entire citizenry and 
enhance democratic legitimacy. 
A robust democracy celebrates diversity and ensures equal representation for all 
citizens. Political parties in Cambodia bear the responsibility of fostering a pluralistic and 
inclusive political landscape. By actively recruiting and nurturing a diverse range of 
candidates, including women, ethnic minorities, and marginalized communities, parties 
can bridge societal divides, promote social cohesion, and establish a government that 
reflects the true fabric of Cambodian society. 
As Cambodia progresses on its democratic journey, it is imperative to recognize 
and support the critical roles that political parties play in shaping a vibrant and responsive 
political system. By fostering an environment conducive to their operation, encouraging 
Contemporary Perspective

Volume IV 
inclusivity, and upholding democratic values, Cambodia can continue to strengthen its 
democratic foundations and fulfill the aspirations of its people. 
And now, with some form of timeline ascertained for the transfer of power, 
Cambodia does indeed has democracy, albeit with its own brand and variety.

Cambodia’s Resilient Democracy 

On Sunday, 23 July 2023, Cambodia achieved yet another landmark in its journey 
towards strengthening its democratic values with a successful election. 
Yesterday, some 8.177 million registered voters or 84.58 percent of the total 
registered voters of 8,213,260 people had cast their ballots in a peaceful and amiable 
manner. Attempts to discourage people from heading to the polls was also foiled. 
This electoral exercise serves as a testament to the unwavering resilience of 
Cambodia’s democracy, demonstrating the country’s commitment to upholding 
democratic principles and fostering political participation. Despite the challenges faced, 
the recent election highlights Cambodia’s determination to forge ahead on its path of 
democratic progress. 
To truly appreciate the significance of the July 2023 election, it is crucial to 
acknowledge Cambodia’s tumultuous history. Emerging from a prolonged period of 
conflict and foreign intervention and occupation, the nation has made remarkable strides 
towards establishing a stable and inclusive democratic system that respects the rights 
and aspirations of its citizens, in which peace and development are the backbones. 
The commitment to conducting free and fair elections demonstrates the 
government’s dedication to upholding democratic principles and ensuring the voice of 
the people is heard. It is a clear signal that Cambodia is determined to strengthen its 
democratic institutions and build a more inclusive society. It is safe to say that the 
democratic values and multi-party system in Cambodia prevail and continue to thrive. No 
forces can change this trend. 
One of the most significant indicators of a vibrant democracy is the participation of 
citizens in the political process. The July 2023 election witnessed a surge in voter 
turnout, exemplifying the increasing engagement and interest of Cambodian citizens in 
shaping their nation’s future. This heightened participation not only strengthens the 
legitimacy of the elected government but also underscores the people’s faith in their 
democratic system. 
A resilient democracy thrives on the diversity of its political landscape. The recent 
election showcased the emergence of a multi-party system, allowing for a broader range 
of voices and perspectives to be represented. There were eighteen political parties 
contested in the election. The presence of multiple political parties fosters healthy 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 11 
Volume IV 
competition and ensures a more balanced governance structure, providing citizens with 
a wider array of choices and platforms to express their political preferences. 
A fundamental pillar of a mature democracy is the peaceful transfer of power. In 
the aftermath of the July 2023 election, Cambodia demonstrated its commitment to this 
principle. The peaceful transition of power reinforces the stability of democratic 
institutions and sets a positive example for future elections. This peaceful handover not 
only strengthens trust within the society but also enhances national resilience and 
political maturity. 
While factional politics and power competition within the ruling party exist, internal 
unity will be likely maintained for the sake of national interest. Notably, over the past five 
hundred years, Cambodia has not had smooth and peaceful power transition. 
While celebrating the resilience of Cambodia’s democracy, it is important to 
acknowledge the challenges that lie ahead. Upholding the integrity of democratic 
institutions, ensuring transparent governance, and safeguarding human rights must 
remain priorities for Cambodia’s leadership. 
Ongoing efforts are required to further strengthen democratic values, promote 
inclusivity, and provide equal opportunities for all citizens. 
While acknowledging the progress made, it is important to recognize that 
Cambodia’s democracy still faces challenges. Upholding the rule of law, ensuring checks 
and balances, and strengthening public service delivery to meet the needs and 
expectations of the people. 
Fighting against corruption remains the most challenging, necessary task. 
Addressing these challenges requires sustained efforts from both the government and 
civil society, as well as support from the international community. 
The international community has a vital role to play in supporting Cambodia’s 
democratic journey. Positive engagement, characterized by constructive dialogue and 
assistance, can help reinforce democratic institutions, promote good governance 
practices, and foster respect for human rights. Building on existing partnerships and 
expanding cooperation will contribute to Cambodia’s continued progress as a democratic 
nation. 
Over 600 international observers from some 60 institutions, including the speaker 
of Dewan Rakyat of Malaysia, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Guinea-Bissa,u and 
Contemporary Perspective

P a g e | 12 
Volume IV 
many former heads of state, heads of government, former presidents and vice presidents 
of the National Assembly, had been accredited for the July 23 National Election. 
This is the transparency of the electoral system, and it is a pre-requisite to 
ascertain the legitimacy of the election despite calls to claim otherwise well before the 
election just because of the absence of one recalcitrant party which wants to be above 
the law, treated as a ‘god’s gift to Cambodian politics’ and under-handed tactics of urging 
voters not to cast their ballots or to invalidate their votes. 
This stupidity, rather than endorsing any of the opposing 17 other parties, shows 
the opposition’s immature style of politics, abetted by their covert and overt supporters 
and financiers. 
As Cambodia continues to address the challenges ahead, it is crucial for the 
government, civil society, and the international community to remain vigilant in 
safeguarding and nurturing Cambodia’s democracy. 
By doing so, Cambodia can build on the achievements of the July 2023 election 
and further strengthen its democratic foundations, ensuring that the voice of its people 
remains central to the nation’s progress and prosperity.

Cambodia’s next leader Hun Manet presents a new era 
for the country’s global relations 

After gaining independence from France in 1953, Cambodia has experienced 
several violent regime changes due to conquest, coups and civil wars. The latest events 
include the 1970 coup, the rise of the Khmer Rouge regime in 1975, a violent power 
transition in 1979 and a violent power struggle in 1997. 
This time, the shift of power has been remarkably peaceful, with Hun Manet set to 
assume the role of prime minister on Aug 22, following the Cambodian People's Party's 
(CPP) victory at the Jul 23 election.  
The reactions to Hun Manet’s appointment have been mixed: On one hand, there 
is optimism that Western-educated Hun Manet may improve Cambodia's testy 
relationship with the West; on the other, there is concern that Hun Sen will still be running 
the show from behind the curtains. 
While it is still early to fully evaluate Hun Manet’s leadership capacity, we can 
glean insights into his worldview from his academic background and over a decade of 
experience as the army chief and head of the CPP youth wing. 
 HOW WILL HUN MANET STEER RELATIONS WITH US AND CHINA? 
Hun Manet, 45, was trained at the West Point military academy in the United 
States and holds a master's degree from New York University and a doctorate from 
Britain's Bristol University, both in economics. 
His exposure to different ideas and approaches is likely to play a role in shaping 
his leadership style in both domestic and international political landscapes. 
The relationship between Cambodia and the US has been tense due to the US' 
interference in Cambodia's democracy and human rights issues. 
After the election, the US derided the polls as “neither free nor fair” and announced 
visa bans on individuals it said had undermined democracy. It also paused several 
foreign assistance programmes in Cambodia.   
“As the ruling Cambodian People’s Party forms a new government, authorities 
have an opportunity to improve the country’s international standing, including by restoring 
genuine multi-party democracy, ending politically motivated trials, reversing convictions 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 14 
Volume IV 
of government critics, and allowing independent media outlets to reopen and function 
without interference,” US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said. 
China, Cambodia’s key partner country, on the other hand congratulated Hun Sen 
on his victory.

Chinese President Xi Jinping in his congratulatory letter.

Hun Manet’s Leadership and Cambodia’s Path 
Towards Progress 

The recent leadership transition in Cambodia marks a significant departure from 
its history of turbulent power transfers. Hun Manet’s peaceful ascension to the role of 
Prime Minister, following the Cambodian People’s Party’s (CPP) landslide victory at the 
July 23 election, sets a positive precedent for the country’s political stability. 
As we look into Hun Manet’s leadership capacity, his academic background and 
experience as the Army Chief and Head of the CPP youth wing offer valuable insights. 
His commitment to engaging with various sources and active listening positions him as 
an informed and receptive decision-maker. This attribute is essential for addressing the 
complex challenges that lie ahead. 
Strategic foresight and scenario analysis are prominent features of Hun Manet’s 
approach. Seeking input from advisors and assistants to explore potential outcomes 
before making critical decisions demonstrates his commitment to finding the best course 
of action, a crucial trait for effective leadership. 
Hun Manet embodies the role of a cautious reformist. Recognizing governance 
challenges in Cambodia, he appears willing to implement necessary reforms while 
ensuring internal unity within the party and government. This pragmatic approach could 
drive positive change while maintaining stability. 
In terms of foreign policy, Hun Manet displays an openness to embracing new 
ideas, particularly in engaging with the West. While Cambodia’s relationship with China 
will remain central, the administration is expected to implement hedging and 
diversification strategies, balancing its external relations. 
Cambodia’s pursuit of an independent foreign policy is a key principle. By making 
autonomous decisions, free from undue external influence, Cambodia seeks to 
determine its diplomatic course based on the nation’s best interests and development. 
This stance preserves Cambodia’s autonomy and sovereignty on the global stage. 
Hun Manet’s administration will prioritize Cambodia’s national strength and 
interests in its foreign policy considerations. Leveraging the country’s resources, 
economic potential, and strategic location will enable the pursuit of opportunities that 
contribute to Cambodia’s development and well-being.

Central to Cambodia’s foreign policy is a commitment to abide by international law 
and norms, promoting stability and predictability in international relations. Engaging in 
open and inclusive multilateralism allows Cambodia to collaborate with other nations and 
find collective solutions to global challenges. 
Economic diplomacy and security are paramount under Hun Manet’s leadership. 
Recognizing the integral role of economics in politics, the government will focus on 
ensuring economic resilience and safeguarding the nation’s interests against external 
threats. 
To enhance economic security, policies will aim to diversify the economy and 
reduce reliance on specific sectors or trade partners. Creating a favorable business 
environment, streamlining regulations, and combating corruption will attract domestic 
and foreign investments. 
Promoting political unity and social cohesion within Cambodia will be a priority. A 
stable domestic political landscape allows the government to focus on economic 
development and international cooperation without internal conflicts hindering progress. 
The path ahead for Cambodia under Hun Manet’s leadership is filled with potential 
and promise. His cautious reformist approach, strategic planning, openness to engaging 
with the international community, and commitment to Cambodia’s interests bode well for 
the nation’s progress. 
As Cambodia charts its path towards the future, the significance of sustained 
observation and assessment cannot be emphasized enough. In the journey of progress, 
challenges are inevitable, necessitating the display of resilience and adaptability by the 
nation’s leadership and its people. However, with a united and thoughtful approach to 
governance, Cambodia holds the potential to emerge as a responsible and esteemed 
member of the global community, firmly committed to advancing on a trajectory of growth 
and development. 
By embracing collective leadership and fostering a sense of unity, Cambodia can 
effectively navigate through the intricacies of its internal and external landscapes. A 
thoughtful leadership, armed with a deep understanding of the nation’s priorities and 
aspirations, can steer the country towards stability and sustainable advancement. This 
will not only solidify Cambodia’s standing in the international arena but also enhance its 
reputation as a reliable partner in global cooperation and development efforts.

As the nation embraces these qualities, it gains the ability to effectively respond to 
challenges and complexities that may arise on its developmental journey. By cultivating 
an environment of stability and progress, Cambodia can attract foreign investments, 
encourage innovation, and bolster economic diversification. In doing so, the nation can 
leverage its vast potential, promoting inclusive growth and prosperity for its citizens. 
Furthermore, by showcasing its commitment to responsible governance and 
cooperative diplomacy, Cambodia can play a more active role in addressing pressing 
global issues. The nation’s active participation in international forums and collaboration 
with other countries can contribute to collective efforts to tackle challenges such as 
climate change, poverty, and public health. 
Cambodia stands at a crucial juncture where visionary and thoughtful leadership 
can propel the nation towards a future of promise and achievement. By embracing 
collective efforts and demonstrating adaptability, Cambodia can foster a legacy of 
sustainable growth and responsible global engagement, solidifying its position as a 
respected member of the global community.

My Cambodian Dream 

As the sun sets on this month, Cambodia is poised to step into a new chapter of 
its history, one defined by ambitious nation-building endeavours. The nation stands at 
the cusp of a transformation that hinges on the development of its human capital- the 
foundation of all. 
Built on the foundations developed by the previous generation, the new generation 
is expected to robustly carry out innovative governance reforms with substantial 
investments in cultivating a knowledge-based economy. 
In my childhood, I nurtured the ambition of becoming a teacher. Yet, this aspiration 
was accompanied by a sense of poignancy and uncertainty. The aftermath of the 
devastation caused by the Khmer Rouge infused my dream of teaching with a deeper 
purpose – it stood as a testament to the undying determination of those who had 
tragically perished, a living tribute to their unrealized aspirations, a torch symbolically 
passed from the fallen to the living. Within this dream, I carried the hopes of those who 
dared to envision a brighter future during the bleakest hours of our history. 
I came into this world, nurtured by the unwavering strength of a single mother, in 
the wake of the Khmer Rouge’s collapse in January 1979. My early years unfolded amid 
a generation marked by the indelible scars of hardship, and my childhood was a canvas 
painted with shades of adversity, uncertainty, and despair. 
The aftermath of a shattered education system loomed before us, a stark mirror 
reflecting the immense devastation that had gripped our nation. In the confines of my 
village nestled in Stoung district, Kompong Thom province, the teachers who survived 
the Khmer Rouge’s brutal reign could be counted on the fingers of one hand, a testament 
to the sheer resilience that had carried them through those harrowing times. 
I could recall walking to school was a perilous endeavour, with the threat of 
landmines lurking on either side of the path. A mere misstep could lead to injury or death, 
a grim reality underscored by the tragic fate of several children who fell victim to the 
remnants of war. 
The spectre of civil war still loomed large, even after the Paris Peace Accord in 
October 1991, with my hometown witnessing the last vestiges of fighting in 1993 during 
an attempt by the Khmer Rouge to disrupt United Nations-supervised elections. The very

Volume IV 
UN peacekeeping forces stationed nearby found themselves besieged- their temporary 
camp located right behind my house. 
In 1992, I encountered two Japanese civilian engineers working under the United 
Nations Transitional Authority (UNTAC)- the first foreigners I had ever met. They stayed 
in a concrete house just in front of our home.  They told me that one day peace would 
eventually return to Cambodia and the road in my district would be rebuilt (national road 
number 6). I smiled, but deep down I was not convinced. 
A decade later, a resurgence of peace began to take hold, heralding an era of 
infrastructure development and incremental socio-economic progress. I managed to 
complete my high school education and ventured abroad for higher studies under various 
scholarships, carrying with me a profound aspiration inspired by those who had taught 
me in the early days, especially my mother and teachers. 
Today, the arc of my journey has taken me from the depths of hopelessness to the 
shores of hopefulness. Having emerged from a period of strife and struggle, I now find 
myself imparting knowledge at various universities around the world. My dream, against 
all odds, has been realized, a testament to the hard-won peace of the late 1990s. 
Surveying the landscape of our achievements and envisioning the road ahead, I 
cannot help but feel a surge of pride for Cambodia’s indomitable spirit and for our ability 
to rebuild a nation from the ashes of the Khmer Rouge’s tyranny. However, our journey 
has not been without its share of missteps and shortcomings. To truly progress, we must 
embrace the wisdom that comes from acknowledging and learning from our mistakes 
and failures. This very process of introspection strengthens our resilience and propels us 
toward better solutions. 
The Cambodian dream that has guided me is one of peace – a dream that has 
been realized but not one that we can afford to take for granted. We must remain vigilant 
in safeguarding the fragile tranquility we have painstakingly nurtured. Yet, another facet 
of this dream lies in the realm of knowledge. To forge a path towards a progressive and 
civilized nation, we must prioritize the development of our human capital, laying the 
foundation for a knowledge-based economy. This path, though arduous, demands 
visionary leadership, transformative actions, and the unwavering participation of each 
and every one of us. We all have a stake here. 
Diversity of opinions and perspectives is the cornerstone of a thriving society. In 
this spirit, I urge each of us to engage in a constructive dialogue that enriches our

understanding and fuels the engines of progress. Constructive criticism, when offered 
with the intent of improvement and growth, is an invaluable tool that can catalyze positive 
change. Let us welcome ideas that challenge the status quo, as they often hold the 
potential to unearth innovative solutions and unearth hidden pathways to success. 
However, as we embrace differing viewpoints, it is paramount that we draw a clear 
line between constructive criticism and destructive comments or behaviors. Destructive 
comments, driven by negativity or animosity, have the potential to undermine the very 
foundation upon which our aspirations are built. Such comments not only hinder progress 
but also sow discord and erode the unity that is essential to our shared journey. Likewise, 
behaviors that seek to disrupt, divide, or derail our collective efforts are antithetical to the 
spirit of nation-building and have no place in the narrative of our future. 
As we look to the horizon, the Cambodian dream beckons us forward – a dream 
rooted in the principles of peace and knowledge. It is a dream that resonates not only 
within the hearts of individuals like myself but within the very soul of our nation. With 
unwavering determination, we shall continue to strive, learn, and grow, ensuring that the 
Cambodian dream flourishes for generations to come.

Five Pillars of Cambodia’s Economic Reforms 

Last month, the dialogue on economic policy among political parties was 
facilitated by the National Election Committee. Within this context, Vongsey Vissoth, a 
prominent figure associated with the Cambodian People’s Party, presented an ambitious 
economic vision – an all-encompassing plan intricately formulated to guide the nation 
towards a more inclusive, sustainable, and resilient economic framework. 
The blueprint outlines five interlinked policy focal points, with each priority echoing 
a resolute dedication from the newly formed administration. It indicates the commitment 
of the new government to construct a socio-economic structure that surpasses mere 
statistical indicators, deeply touching upon the essence of people’s well-being. 
The roadmap plots a course towards a future characterized by increased 
prosperity and resilience, adroitly navigating the intricate currents of economic 
complexities and uncertainties both domestically and internationally. 
Anticipated to be a potent instrument for ushering in a transformative wave of 
positive change, this roadmap is poised to uplift individuals, families, and communities 
towards better livelihoods and a more promising horizon. 
 Ensuring Macroeconomic and Financial Stability 
At the core of Cambodia’s economic strategy lies the imperative to maintain 
macroeconomic and financial stability. This entails a multi-faceted approach, 
encompassing measures to curb inflation, stabilize exchange rates, balance the national 
budget, and secure the resilience of both traditional banks and emerging non-bank 
financial institutions. These foundational steps create a solid platform upon which 
subsequent growth initiatives can flourish. 
 Fostering Inclusive and Resilient Economic Growth 
A standout objective of Cambodia’s vision is the pursuit of robust, inclusive 
economic growth as a means to alleviate poverty. The spotlight here falls on empowering 
small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), fortifying the informal economy, harnessing 
the potential of digital technologies, and prioritizing sustainable “green” development. By 
nurturing a diverse range of economic drivers, Cambodia aims to not only raise its GDP 
but also ensure that the benefits of growth are widely shared.

An integral component of the plan centres on optimizing the management of the 
national budget. The government has charted a course towards fiscal efficiency and

seeks to enhance revenue management within the national budget, thereby maximizing 
resource mobilization. The outcome promises to be a judicious allocation of funds that 
fuels development projects across the spectrum.

Recognizing the pivotal role of a robust financial sector in propelling economic 
progress, Cambodia has identified this as one of priority areas. A central objective 
revolves around facilitating the seamless channelling of national savings into priority 
sectors through increased efficiency. Diversification of financial products, bolstering 
financial inclusivity, embracing financial technology, and innovative financing 
mechanisms such as sovereign bonds, collectively underscore the nation’s commitment 
to nurturing a dynamic financial ecosystem. 
 Empowering the Private Sector 
The plan rounds off with a resolute focus on elevating the private sector to the 
vanguard of economic growth. By cultivating a business-friendly environment, Cambodia 
seeks to unleash the full potential of private enterprise. This entails initiatives aimed at 
attracting investments, fostering collaboration within regional and global economies, and 
streamlining public services to better support private sector enterprises. The emphasis 
on this sector serves as a testament to Cambodia’s belief in the entrepreneurial spirit as 
a driving force or engine behind economic growth. 
The bedrock upon which the realization of these five pivotal pillars stands is the 
cultivation of human capital, the ignition of innovation, seamless coordination between 
state entities, and the nurturing of robust public-private-people partnerships.

The true potential of any economic agenda lies within the capabilities, skills, and 
aspirations of its people. As Cambodia sets its sights on the horizon of sustainable 
growth, the development of its human capital takes centre stage. Investing in education, 
skill enhancement, and fostering a culture of lifelong learning becomes paramount. By

approach not only bolsters economic endeavours but also nurtures a sense of collective

Hun Manet’s Evolving Foreign Policy Doctrine 

The world is watching as Cambodia navigates the complex web of international 
affairs. In an era marked by trust deficit, fast-evolving global power shift and transforming 
geopolitical and geo-economic landscapes, Cambodia finds itself compelled to take an 
active and forward-looking stance in its foreign affairs—an approach that seeks 
friendship with all nations while harboring no adversaries. 
The Asia Pacific region is at an inflection point- facing an arc of geopolitical 
instability. Regional security flashpoints such as the tensions on the Korean Peninsula, 
Taiwan Straits, East and South China Seas, and Myanmar crisis continue to threaten 
regional peace and stability. Against this backdrop, Cambodia must be prepared to face 
different scenarios, while taking a leadership role in international crisis prevention and 
management by prioritizing diplomacy, dialogue and international law. 
It has been slightly more than a month since Prime Minister Hun Manet assumed 
office. In his inaugural month, Hun Manet embarked on a whirlwind diplomatic journey, 
which included attending the ASEAN Summit and related Summits in Indonesia, making 
his first official visit to China, where he also participated in the China-ASEAN Expo, and 
addressing the 78th UNGA in New York. 
These high-level engagements provided him with invaluable opportunities to raise 
the Cambodian flag and connect with a diverse array of global stakeholders, ranging 
from political leaders and chief diplomats to business leaders and thought leaders. 
The key question that arises is what we can discern from Prime Minister Hun 
Manet’s foreign policy doctrine. 
 Independence 
One of the central tenets of Hun Manet’s foreign policy doctrine appears to be a 
commitment to an independent and non-aligned stance. This approach underscores 
Cambodia’s determination to steer its own course in international affairs, free from 
external pressures or alignments. In an era where geopolitical rivalries loom large, this 
emphasis on autonomy is a notable cornerstone of Cambodia’s foreign policy. 
Addressing the 78th United Nations General Assembly, he reaffirmed Cambodia’s 
consistent and firm stand to neither host foreign military bases on its soil nor allow its 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 27 
Volume IV 
territory to be used against a third country. This non-alignment stance is deeply rooted in 
Cambodia’s history and its struggle for self-determination. 
Throughout its tumultuous past, Cambodia has strived to maintain a position of 
neutrality in international conflicts, seeking to avoid entanglements in the disputes of 
others while adhering to international law. This policy serves as a foundation for peaceful 
coexistence with neighboring nations. 
 Multilateralism 
Another defining feature of Hun Manet’s vision is the unwavering commitment to 
multilateralism. The 21st century has witnessed the rise of complex global challenges 
that transcend national borders. From climate crisis to the pandemic crisis, these issues 
necessitate collaborative, cross-border solutions. Unilateralism and block politics are ill-
suited to address these complex and interlinked challenges. 
Multilateralism is fundamentally rooted in the concept of shared responsibility and 
collective action. It acknowledges that global challenges require coordinated efforts, 
shared responsibilities, and pooled resources from multiple nations. 
ASEAN remains the cornerstone of Cambodia’s foreign policy. It reflects a 
strategic vision that prioritizes regional stability, prosperity, and cooperation. Embracing 
ASEAN-led initiatives like RCEP and AOIP, Cambodia aims to leverage regional 
partnerships and frameworks to enhance its economic growth, diplomatic engagement, 
and resilience in the face of emerging challenges. By doing so, Cambodia not only 
strengthens its regional standing but also contributes to the broader mission of ASEAN 
in building a resilient, sustainable, and inclusive community. 
 International Law 
Lastly, Hun Manet’s foreign policy doctrine firmly aligns with the concept of a 
rules-based international order- referring to a system of global governance in which 
international relations and interactions are guided by a set of agreed rules, norms, 
principles, and institutions. These rules are established to promote peaceful coexistence, 
cooperation, and peaceful settlement of disputes. 
By adhering to the established international norms and standards, Cambodia 
envisions to be a responsible, reliable, and principled member of the international 
community that is genuinely committed to upholding the principles enshrined in the 
United Nations Charter. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 28 
Volume IV 
Embracing a rules-based order also entails strengthening and supporting 
international institutions such as the United Nations and ASEAN. Cambodia’s active 
participation in these forums reinforces its political will and leadership to address cross-
border challenges. 
 Cambodia First 
At the heart of foreign policy lies core national interests, which include economic 
prosperity, security, stability, and the well-being of the people. Notably, economics 
determines politics. Cambodia seeks economic growth, access to markets, attract 
foreign investments, and reach favorable trade agreements to enhance their prosperity 
and the standard of living for the people so that Cambodia could realize its vision to 
become a high-income country by 2050. 
Crafting foreign policy is an intricate and multifaceted undertaking that demands a 
deep comprehension of national and international megatrends, core national interests, 
and the intricate interplay and delicate balance among these interests. There is a need 
to enhance the capacity to analyze evolving international structural dynamics and 
anticipate diverse potential scenarios, and the competence to navigate through 
challenges which ultimately can develop innovative solutions and breakthroughs. 
As Prime Minister Hun Manet is thriving to navigate Cambodia in an increasingly 
complex, uncertain, and volatile world, it will be intriguing to observe how these three key 
strategic principles – independence, multilateralism, and a rules-based international 
order – shape Cambodia’s foreign policy direction. These principles are not just a 
roadmap for Cambodia’s international role but also a testament to its commitment to 
being a responsible and respected member of the international community.

Innovation 

In a world grappling with mounting humanitarian challenges, the 20th Southeast 
Asia Red Cross and Red Crescent Leaders Meeting and the 2nd Southeast Asia Youth 
Forum held in Phnom Penh last week served as a platform of partnership building and 
innovation. 
Hosted by the Cambodian Red Cross and attended by eleven Red Cross and Red 
Crescent national societies from Southeast Asia, the International Federation of Red 
Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and 
the ASEAN Secretariat, this annual meeting marked another critical turning point in the 
humanitarian sector. 
This annual meeting aims to discuss Red Cross and Red Crescent policies and 
issues, assess progress in strategic directions, foster sub-regional cooperation and 
accountability, strengthen collaboration, enhance performance, align with global 
commitments, and ensure adequate follow-up on the agreed commitments. 
In her opening address, Samdech Kittiprittpundit Bun Rany Hun Sen, President of 
the Cambodian Red Cross (CRC), emphasized the critical need for cultivating innovative 
solutions to tackle humanitarian issues and challenges, particularly in optimizing the 
utilization of scarce resources and impacting more people. 
As the critical outcome of the meeting, the Phnom Penh Statement was issued to 
highlight the progress made and set forth new directions, while underscoring the 
importance of building partnerships and leveraging the responsibility and privilege to 
impact changes. 
The statement commended the relentless efforts of the Cambodian Red Cross in 
championing humanitarian innovation while encouraging knowledge sharing and the 
professional development of our youth in the domains of humanitarian innovation and 
public communication. 
Humanitarian innovation is not an abstract concept but a tangible force for positive 
change. The Phnom Penh Statement is a testament to our collective commitment to 
advancing innovation, fostering collaboration, and empowering the youth who will carry 
the torch forward. Together, we are paving the way for a more resilient, inclusive, and 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 30 
Volume IV 
sustainable future where the most vulnerable among us receive the support and care 
they deserve. 
 The Imperative of Humanitarian Innovation 
Humanitarian innovation has emerged as an indispensable tool for addressing 
these complex challenges as the world grapples with multifaceted crises ranging from 
the pandemic to climate crisis, natural disasters, and protracted conflicts. 
It is a dynamic force that offers creative and sustainable solutions, substantially 
enhancing the effectiveness of humanitarian responses, empowering communities, and 
contributing to constructing a more resilient and inclusive society. 
The core premise of humanitarian innovation is rooted in the idea that conventional 
approaches are no longer sufficient to meet the evolving needs of vulnerable populations. 
It challenges us to think outside the box, to embrace technological advancements, and 
to engage in proactive problem-solving. The Cambodian Red Cross has exemplified this 
ethos, leading the way in adopting innovative approaches to humanitarian action. 
 Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration 
The significance of multi-stakeholder collaboration and partnership building 
cannot be overstated in a world characterized by interconnectivity. The strategic 
partnership between the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies in Southeast 
Asia and the ASEAN Secretariat, particularly in addressing natural disasters, is a 
testament to collective action’s power. 
The challenges posed by natural disasters, exacerbated by climate change, 
require a coordinated and harmonized response. By aligning their resources and efforts, 
these organizations can better mobilize and allocate resources to meet the urgent needs 
of affected communities. It underscores the notion that we can achieve far more when 
working together than when working in isolation. 
 Leading by Example 
The Cambodian Red Cross has emerged as a trailblazer in humanitarian 
innovation, inspiring others to follow. Its unwavering commitment to harnessing the 
power of innovation is not merely a testament to its dedication to Cambodia but also 
lessons learned for other humanitarian organizations. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 31 
Volume IV 
One of the Cambodian Red Cross’s most notable achievements is its 
implementation of various humanitarian innovation projects. These initiatives have 
ranged from effectively delivering Covid-19 vaccines to vulnerable groups to providing 
remote and marginalized areas with access to safe drinking water. The construction of 
climate-resilient housing further illustrates the organization’s commitment to addressing 
pressing needs and building long-term resilience. 
 Empowering Local Response 
A cornerstone of the Cambodian Red Cross’s approach has been decentralization, 
which empowers and enables local provincial committees to respond to humanitarian 
issues in their respective localities. This model, grounded in local resources, knowledge, 
and community engagement, has proven highly effective. It ensures that responses are 
swift and contextually relevant, reflecting the specific needs and challenges faced by 
local populations. 
The convergence of innovation, collaboration, youth empowerment, and 
localization can reshape the humanitarian landscape. Innovation knows no boundaries, 
and compassion transcends borders. Leading with innovation demonstrates that our 
collective efforts can bring about lasting humanitarian impacts. 
In the spirit of unity and humanitarianism, let us move forward with determination, 
fully aware that our collective efforts can shape a brighter, more inclusive, and 
sustainable future for all. As an African proverb wisely reminds us, ‘If you want to go fast, 
go alone; if you want to go far, go together.’ Red Cross and Red Cresent for all; all for 
Red Cross and Red Cresent. Let’s keep the momentum of the movement.

Cambodia’s Funan Techo Canal, A Game Changer? 

Cambodia, a nation rich in history, culture and natural resources, has long been a 
land of opportunities and untapped potential. 
Over the past three decades, after gaining total peace in 1999, the country has 
been making strides towards economic growth and poverty reduction. 
One of the most ambitious and transformative projects on Cambodia’s horizon is 
the Funan Techo Canal, a colossal endeavor that could reshape the country’s future. 
 Why is it named Funan? 
Funan, an ancient state influenced by Indian culture and located in the Mekong 
Delta, flourished from the 1st to the 6th century AD. It featured an intricate network of 
canals linking its economic core to coastal regions, which together formed the main area 
of Funan. Angkor Borey was the hub of economic and cultural activities during this era. 
As such, Funan represents an example of economic and cultural interconnection. 
Funan Techo Canal project can be regarded as Cambodia’s endeavor to transform 
itself to be the economic and cultural gateway of the Mekong. 
The project was approved at the 6th Plenary Session of the National Assembly on 
19 May 2023. On 7 June 2023, the government decided to establish an inter-ministerial 
commission to implement the project. On 17 October 2023, Cambodia signed an 
agreement to allow China Bridge and Road Corporation (CRBC) to conduct a feasibility 
study on the project. 
Stretching 180 kilometers from the Takeo canal of the Mekong River to the coastal 
province of Kep, the canal traverses four provinces: Kandal, Takeo, Kampot, and Kep. 
This waterway is set to be a game-changer for Cambodia, and here’s why. 
The Funan Techo Canal is designed to be a remarkable engineering feat. With a 
width of 100 meters upstream and 80 meters downstream, and a depth of 5.4 meters, it 
will accommodate two-way traffic and can carry ships with up to 3000DWT (Deadweight 
Tonnage). The canal is built to international standards, prioritizing safety and quality in its 
construction. 
One of the notable aspects of this project is the thoroughness of the planning and 
the environmental considerations. A serious study was conducted by the government 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 33 
Volume IV 
before project approval, taking more than two years of technical, legal, economic, 
environmental, and social studies and inter-ministerial consultations. 
This comprehensive approach ensures that the canal will not only benefit the 
economy but also help preserve the ecology and environmental balance of the region. 
While it is acknowledged that some environmental impacts may occur during 
construction, measures will be taken to mitigate them. 
The Funan Techo Canal is not just a grand infrastructure project; it’s a lifeline for 
approximately 1.6 million people living along its route. By facilitating efficient 
transportation and trade, it promises to bring economic opportunities to these 
communities. 
The project aligns with Article 5 of the Mekong Agreement of 1995, which 
mandates that projects on tributaries of the Mekong River, including the Funan Techo 
Canal, must be subject to notification to the Joint Committee. Cambodia has duly 
complied with this requirement, demonstrating its commitment to regional cooperation 
and sustainable development. 
The estimated cost of constructing the canal is a staggering USD 1.7 billion, a 
significant investment in Cambodia’s future. However, this investment is expected to 
yield substantial returns. The canal is projected to cut transport costs significantly, with 
savings of approximately USD170 for a 20-foot container and USD 223 for a 40-foot 
container, reducing transport costs by about 16%. 
This will not only benefit businesses but also consumers, as lower transport costs 
can translate into more affordable goods. 
The Funan Techo Canal is expected to boost the country’s fourth major economic 
center. This new development joins the ranks of existing three key economic regions: the 
first being Phnom Penh and its neighboring areas, known for their vibrant urban 
economy; the second is Sihanoukville along with its adjacent regions, noted for their 
strategic coastal economic activities; and the third is Siem Reap and its surrounding 
locales, renowned for their cultural and tourism-driven economy. 
The economic internal rate of return, according to the study of the government, is 
calculated to be between 20% and 31%, indicating its potential for profitability and 
economic growth. The canal’s impact will extend beyond its immediate vicinity. It will 
promote the development of industrial zones, the formation of production lines, and 
supply chains, particularly in the agriculture and aquaculture sectors. Moreover, the 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part I: Cambodia 
P a g e | 34 
Volume IV 
canal will spur urbanization along the waterway, contributing to the development of what 
is being referred to as the fourth economic pole. 
Clearly, the project will improve transportation networks and bring new 
opportunities to communities along its route. In this regard, relevant stakeholders, 
including the government, private sector, and local communities, must work together to 
ensure the Funan Techo Canal becomes a model of national and regional economic 
integration and connectivity as well as the promotion of inclusive, resilient and 
sustainable development.

Dispute, The Unfinished Story
