Cambodia’s Economic Outlook 

Cambodia’s economic performance in 2024 has shown resilience, with an 
estimated growth rate of approximately 6 percent. While there are slight variations in 
growth rate estimates, the overall outlook remains positive. According to the World Bank, 
the primary drivers of this growth include the revival of goods and services exports, a 
rebound in tourism, and the recovery of private consumption, all of which have 
underpinned a stronger domestic economic recovery. 
The manufacturing sector continues to play a pivotal role in Cambodia’s growth, 
with notable contributions from the garment, footwear, and travel goods industries. These 
sectors have not only powered economic expansion but also supported employment and 
export earnings. In agriculture, growth was recorded at 1.2 percent in 2024, with 
projections suggesting a modest increase to 1.3 percent in 2025. The services sector 
performed strongly with a 5.4 percent growth rate in 2024, though it is anticipated to 
slightly decelerate to 5.2 percent in 2025. Conversely, the real estate and property 
investment sectors remain subdued, reflecting broader global economic uncertainties. 
Looking ahead, Cambodia’s economic growth is expected to slightly exceed 6 
percent in 2025, buoyed by continued recovery in key sectors. However, this positive 
trajectory faces several risks. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has highlighted 
vulnerabilities stemming from weaker growth in major global economies such as the 
People’s Republic of China, Europe, and the United States. 
Additional challenges include high levels of private debt, volatile global fuel prices, 
and the severe impacts of extreme weather events driven by climate change. 
At the core of Cambodia’s economic challenges lies relatively low productivity, 
which is hampered by several structural issues. These include weak governance 
systems, insufficient innovation, a shortage of skilled labor, low levels of technological 
adoption, and limited integration into both national and international production networks. 
Furthermore, Cambodia’s high ranking on corruption indices, compared to other 
Southeast Asian nations, has deterred some foreign investors. The absence of robust 
and transparent institutions, particularly within the justice system and law enforcement 
agencies, exacerbates this problem. 
Additionally, Cambodia faces competitiveness challenges due to high electricity 
and logistics costs, which remain uncompetitive compared to neighboring countries. The

skills gap in the labor market further compounds these issues, limiting the country’s 
ability to attract and retain high-value investments. Addressing these structural 
weaknesses is imperative for Cambodia to sustain and enhance its economic growth 
trajectory. 
To strengthen its economic outlook, Cambodia must prioritize reforms in 
governance, improve institutional transparency, and enhance its investment and 
business climate. By addressing infrastructure bottlenecks, investing in skill development, 
and fostering innovation, the country can unlock its economic potential and secure long-
term growth amidst a challenging global economic environment partially caused 
protectionism, isolationism and unilateralism. 
Concerning governance reforms, several critical factors must come into play to 
ensure meaningful progress: strategic guidance, strategic focus, bold leadership, 
effective public service delivery, and a sound Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) 
mechanism. 
Governance reforms cannot be piecemeal or superficial; they require a 
comprehensive and transformative approach. Strategic guidance ensures that reforms 
are aligned with long-term national goals, while strategic focus prioritizes key areas that 
yield the greatest impact for the people. 
Without bold leadership, reforms risk being derailed by entrenched interests, 
bureaucratic inertia, or fear of challenging the status quo. Effective public service delivery 
must be the centerpiece of these efforts, as the quality of governance is ultimately judged 
by its tangible impact on citizens’ daily lives. A robust Monitoring and Evaluation 
mechanism is essential for tracking progress, identifying bottlenecks, and ensuring 
accountability at every level of implementation. 
It is time to conduct what can be described as “institutional surgery”—a deliberate, 
targeted, and courageous restructuring of governance systems to remove inefficiencies, 
eliminate corruption, and enhance performance. This requires leaders with bold and 
courageous vision, who are willing to champion reforms even in the face of resistance. 
Institutional surgery must prioritize the principles of meritocracy, ensuring that 
appointments and promotions are based on competence, integrity, and performance. It 
must also focus on building institutions that are strong, smart, and clean, capable of 
adapting to changing demands, leveraging innovation, and upholding ethical standards.

At the heart of these reforms lies the imperative to improve public service delivery. 
Improved livelihoods, justice, and better public services are not mere aspirations—they 
are fundamental rights of the people. Citizens deserve access to services that are 
efficient, inclusive, and equitable, whether in healthcare, education, infrastructure, or 
social protection. 
Political leaders at both the national and sub-national levels must take decisive 
action to address these demands. They bear the ultimate responsibility to improve 
people’s lives, promote social justice, and ensure that governance serves its highest 
purpose: the well-being of the Cambodian people. This requires not only vision and 
policy innovation but also the ability to inspire and mobilize all stakeholders—public 
officials, private sector partners, and civil society actors—toward a shared mission of 
delivering results for the people.

Cambodia’s economic performance in 2024 has shown resilience, with an 
estimated growth rate of approximately 6 percent. While there are slight variations in 
growth rate estimates, the overall outlook remains positive. According to the World Bank, 
the primary drivers of this growth include the revival of goods and services exports, a 
rebound in tourism, and the recovery of private consumption, all of which have 
underpinned a stronger domestic economic recovery. 
The manufacturing sector continues to play a pivotal role in Cambodia’s growth, 
with notable contributions from the garment, footwear, and travel goods industries. These 
sectors have not only powered economic expansion but also supported employment and 
export earnings. In agriculture, growth was recorded at 1.2 percent in 2024, with 
projections suggesting a modest increase to 1.3 percent in 2025. The services sector 
performed strongly with a 5.4 percent growth rate in 2024, though it is anticipated to 
slightly decelerate to 5.2 percent in 2025. Conversely, the real estate and property 
investment sectors remain subdued, reflecting broader global economic uncertainties. 
Looking ahead, Cambodia’s economic growth is expected to slightly exceed 6 
percent in 2025, buoyed by continued recovery in key sectors. However, this positive 
trajectory faces several risks. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has highlighted 
vulnerabilities stemming from weaker growth in major global economies such as the 
People’s Republic of China, Europe, and the United States. 
Additional challenges include high levels of private debt, volatile global fuel prices, 
and the severe impacts of extreme weather events driven by climate change. 
At the core of Cambodia’s economic challenges lies relatively low productivity, 
which is hampered by several structural issues. These include weak governance 
systems, insufficient innovation, a shortage of skilled labor, low levels of technological 
adoption, and limited integration into both national and international production networks. 
Furthermore, Cambodia’s high ranking on corruption indices, compared to other 
Southeast Asian nations, has deterred some foreign investors. The absence of robust 
and transparent institutions, particularly within the justice system and law enforcement 
agencies, exacerbates this problem. 
Additionally, Cambodia faces competitiveness challenges due to high electricity 
and logistics costs, which remain uncompetitive compared to neighboring countries. The

governance, improve institutional transparency, and enhance its investment and 
business climate. By addressing infrastructure bottlenecks, investing in skill development,

Concerning governance reforms, several critical factors must come into play to 
ensure meaningful progress: strategic guidance, strategic focus, bold leadership,

comprehensive and transformative approach. Strategic guidance ensures that reforms 
are aligned with long-term national goals, while strategic focus prioritizes key areas that

bureaucratic inertia, or fear of challenging the status quo. Effective public service delivery

mechanism is essential for tracking progress, identifying bottlenecks, and ensuring 
accountability at every level of implementation.

ASEAN-China Partnership in a New Era 

Geographical proximity, civilizational connectivity, economic 
interdependence and common security ensure that this collaboration 
remains dynamic and enduring 
The global landscape is swiftly evolving into a multiplex world defined by multiple 
modernities, diverse civilizations and multiple power centers. This is an interconnected 
and interdependent world where both state and non-state actors interact to shape the 
emerging international order. The relationship between the Association of Southeast 
Asian Nations and China is evolving within this dynamic. 
The geographical proximity between the ASEAN member states and China has 
served as a foundation in shaping their relations and facilitating frequent interactions, 
exchanges and cooperation at various levels. This proximity has not only encouraged 
the development of robust diplomatic ties but has also allowed for the easy movement of 
people, goods and ideas between the ASEAN members and China. The shared land 
borders, maritime routes and immediate regional presence have created an environment 
conducive to sustained engagement and collaboration, fostering a sense of familiarity 
and mutual understanding. 
Two decades have passed since China ratified the Treaty of Amity and 
Cooperation with ASEAN. This milestone provides an opportune moment to reflect on 
the development of the ASEAN-China partnership, and the contributions China has 
made toward fostering regional peace and stability. Over the years, the strategic 
cooperation between the ASEAN and China has yielded significant achievements and 
demonstrated the potential for mutually beneficial collaboration. 
China's adherence to the principles of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation has 
played a significant role in maintaining peace and stability in the region. China's 
willingness to engage in dialogue and collaborate with the ASEAN members has helped 
build confidence, reduce tensions and establish a foundation for peaceful coexistence. 
While remarkable progress has been made, challenges remain in the ASEAN-
China partnership. Addressing territorial disputes in the South China Sea and ensuring 
the effective implementation of existing agreements will require continued commitment 
and dialogue. Maintaining transparency, adhering to international law, and promoting 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 156 
Volume IV 
peaceful resolution mechanisms will be essential to building trust and confidence 
between ASEAN and China. 
One of the key achievements of the ASEAN-China partnership has been the 
establishment of a robust economic relationship. China has emerged as ASEAN's largest 
trading partner since 2009, with trade volumes increasing over the years. Last year, the 
bilateral trade volume hit $975.3 billion. The ASEAN-China Free Trade Area has 
contributed to the expansion of trade and investment, benefiting both sides. Version 3.0 
of ACFTA negotiations was officially launched early this year to further liberalize and 
facilitate bilateral trade flow. 
ACFTA 3.0 is set to synergize harmoniously with the Regional Comprehensive 
Economic Partnership and other collaborative economic and trade mechanisms within 
the region. This dynamic partnership aims to propel the region into a thriving epicenter of 
growth that is marked by openness, inclusivity and shared prosperity. 
Currently, over 90 percent of goods (approximately 7,000 types) benefit from tariff-
free treatment between China and ASEAN. The upcoming ACFTA 3.0 aims to further 
reduce tariffs, establish regulations in areas such as customs, inspections, and 
quarantine, and enhance the liberalization and simplification of trade and investment. 
This will also result in better safeguarding of consumer rights and interests on both sides, 
fostering the growth of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and generating 
additional employment opportunities. 
Beyond economic ties, the ASEAN-China partnership has fostered vibrant people-
to-people exchanges. Cultural events, educational programs and tourism initiatives have 
facilitated greater understanding, appreciation, and friendship between ASEAN and 
China. These interactions have not only strengthened societal bonds but also paved the 
way for enhanced cooperation in various sectors such as education, science and 
technology and tourism. 
Connectivity lies at the heart of ASEAN-China cooperation, promoting trade, 
tourism and people-to-people exchanges. China's Belt and Road Initiative has provided 
a platform for infrastructure development and connectivity projects in the region. 
Collaborative initiatives, such as the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Mechanism, have 
strengthened regional connectivity, enhancing transportation and fostering cross-border 
cooperation. China's commitment to investing in infrastructure has boosted connectivity 
within ASEAN and beyond, facilitating economic integration and regional development. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 157 
Volume IV 
ASEAN and China have also deepened their cooperation in non-traditional 
security areas, such as counter-terrorism, disaster management and transnational crime. 
Joint exercises, information-sharing mechanisms and capacity-building initiatives have 
strengthened regional responses to common challenges. China's active participation in 
these areas has facilitated knowledge sharing, technical assistance and resource 
mobilization, contributing to the overall resilience and security of the region. 
While significant progress has been made in the ASEAN-China partnership, there 
are areas where further cooperation can bring mutual benefits. Continued efforts should 
focus on strengthening people-to-people exchanges, fostering cultural understanding, 
and promoting sustainable development. Environmental cooperation, technology sharing 
and digital connectivity are promising avenues for deepening collaboration. By building 
on past achievements, ASEAN and China can unlock the immense potential for shared 
prosperity, greater regional integration and sustainable development. 
As the ASEAN members and China navigate future challenges, it is crucial to 
sustain the positive momentum, reinforce mutual trust and continue to work together to 
ensure a peaceful and prosperous future for the region. The ASEAN-China partnership 
serves as a shining example of cooperation and diplomacy in an increasingly 
interconnected world. 
The binding factors of ASEAN-China relations — geographical proximity, 
civilizational connectivity, economic interdependence, and common security — 
complement and reinforce each other, forming a multifaceted foundation for a dynamic 
and enduring partnership. These factors not only facilitate practical cooperation but also 
promote a sense of shared destiny, fostering an environment where mutual interests are 
pursued, challenges are collectively addressed, and a true community with a shared 
future can be realized.

Is the ASEAN–Japan relationship fit for the times? 

 In Brief 
The ASEAN–Japan relationship today is almost unrecognizable from that of 50 
years ago when riots against the visits of former Japanese prime minister Kakuei Tanaka 
to Southeast Asian capitals were emblematic of its troubled state. Japan’s current benign 
role in ASEAN belies what has been a powerful alignment of interests and influence 
assiduously developed over the ensuing decades important to the relationship’s success. 
The question is how these foundations fit the present relationship. The 50th 
anniversary of the ASEAN–Japan dialogue underscores the strong ties that have been 
built in the intervening decades. But a fast-evolving, multiplex world order, with new 
centres of power and increasingly complex interactions, poses a number of challenges 
to the relationship going forward. 
Intense geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China presents 
unprecedented challenges for ASEAN, and Japan will need to cooperate with heightened 
awareness and strategic acumen to address these challenges. The relationship with 
Japan is also a key element in the environment in which ASEAN will have to navigate the 
strategic dilemma between the United States and China. 
Navigating the balance between China and the United States is crucial for 
maintaining regional stability and upholding ASEAN’s shared principles of openness and 
inclusivity. As Japan tilts towards its US alliance, balancing competing interests, avoiding 
ASEAN’s overreliance on any single power and preserving centrality and strategic 
autonomy will require continuing and deft diplomatic initiative. 
Managing these complexities through dialogue, trust-building and a focus on 
shared interests is key. Addressing challenges to the ASEAN–Japan relationship, like 
regional power dynamics, territorial disputes, economic competition and historical 
tensions will be essential for fostering a more resilient and cooperative partnership. 
Japan’s commitment to regional security and engagement in multilateral 
frameworks provides avenues for closer collaboration with ASEAN, under the framework 
of the East Asia Summit, the ASEAN Regional Forum, the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ 
Meeting Plus and the ASEAN Expanded Maritime Forum. But Japan’s involvement in 
security minilaterals such as the Quad—which China views as a containment strategy—
does not sit comfortably with ASEAN. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 159 
Volume IV 
Compatibility between Japan’s Free and Open Indo-Pacific and the ASEAN 
Outlook on the Indo-Pacific lies in their shared objectives and overlapping principles. 
Both emphasise a rules-based international order, respect for sovereignty and the 
promotion of connectivity and economic integration. Through mutual collaboration, these 
initiatives have the potential to contribute significantly to peace, stability and economic 
development in the Asia-Pacific region, but how these agendas evolve, are defined and 
made operational is still a work in progress. 
The sharing of intelligence, expertise and best practice has enabled a more 
comprehensive approach to countering radicalization, preventing terrorist financing and 
enhancing border security. By pooling resources and knowledge, Japan and ASEAN 
have bolstered their respective counterterrorism capabilities and contributed to regional 
stability. In 2014, ASEAN and Japan adopted a Joint Declaration for Cooperation to 
Combat Terrorism and Transnational Crime to strengthen cooperation in this area. 
Given the importance of maritime domains in the region, ensuring security and 
freedom of navigation has been an area of collaboration between Japan and ASEAN. 
Japan actively supports ASEAN member states in enhancing their maritime capabilities, 
providing assistance in areas such as maritime domain awareness, capacity building, 
joint exercises and equipment. 
Since the 1970s Japan has supplied surveillance ships to nations within ASEAN, 
including Vietnam and Indonesia. It has also financially supported various initiatives 
aimed at enhancing the capabilities of ASEAN nations to prevent and counteract unlawful 
fishing activities. In 2017, Japan entered into a collaborative agreement with Thailand, 
focusing on combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. This agreement 
emphasized improving the traceability of fishery products and bolstering efforts in 
monitoring, controlling and overseeing fishing operations. 
With Japan and several ASEAN countries prone to natural disasters, sharing 
expertise and resources in disaster response and recovery is another significant area of 
collaboration. Japan’s experience with disaster preparedness, early warning systems 
and post-disaster reconstruction is instrumental in assisting ASEAN member states with 
capacity building to mitigate the impact of natural disasters. This cooperation has not 
only saved lives but also promoted regional solidarity and cooperation in times of crisis. 
Economic ties between ASEAN and Japan have flourished over the years, with 
Japan remaining one of ASEAN’s largest trading partners and a major source of foreign 
direct investment (FDI). FDI outflows from Japan to ASEAN amounted to around US$20 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 160 
Volume IV 
billion and bilateral trade reached US$240.2 billion in 2022. ASEAN is home to 30 per 
cent of all Japanese overseas subsidiaries. The ASEAN–Japan Comprehensive 
Economic Partnership has facilitated trade liberalization, market access and economic 
integration. Infrastructure development, such as the Partnership for Quality Infrastructure, 
also received active support from Japan, contributing to ASEAN’s connectivity goals. 
ASEAN and Japan can focus on enhancing physical and digital connectivity, 
promoting trade facilitation, strengthening regional supply chains and addressing climate 
change and sustainable development. Continued support from Japan is crucial to ensure 
inclusive growth and bridge development disparities among ASEAN member states. The 
Japan–ASEAN Integration Fund, established in 2006, and Japan–Mekong Cooperation, 
founded in 2008, are the two such mechanisms established to assist the least developed 
economies in ASEAN. 
Deepening people-to-people ties through cultural exchanges, educational 
programs and tourism will further foster mutual understanding and friendship. 
Strengthening educational cooperation and providing reciprocal scholarships for students 
from Japan and ASEAN nations will also contribute to long-term relationship building. 
ASEAN and Japan need to continue working closely together to strengthen open 
and inclusive multilateralism, promoting a rules-based international order and leveraging 
opportunities for economic integration, security cooperation and people-to-people 
exchanges. In this way, ASEAN and Japan can navigate the challenges and build a 
stronger and more sustainable relationship in the years to come.

Republic of Korea’s Regional Activism 

The Asia-Pacific region is undergoing a profound and multifaceted transformation 
that fundamentally reshapes its geopolitical and geo-economic landscape. This 
transformation is characterized by a web of interconnected factors collectively redefining 
the region’s dynamics. These factors include intensifying geopolitical rivalries, regional 
and global supply chain disruptions, a sluggish economic recovery, and the emergence 
of various non-traditional security threats, such as the climate crisis and natural 
disasters. 
Amidst Southeast Asia’s myriad of challenges and pressures, the region remains 
steadfast in its pursuit of regional integration and connectivity. This unwavering 
commitment is a testament to Southeast Asia’s aspiration to retain its status as an 
epicentrum of growth and economic dynamism within the broader Asia-Pacific region. 
In this context, the Republic of Korea (ROK) unveiled a strategic vision known as 
the Korea-ASEAN Solidarity Initiative (KASI) at the ASEAN-ROK Summit held in Phnom 
Penh last year. This initiative marks a shift in the ROK’s foreign policy approach, focusing 
on fostering a free, peaceful, and prosperous Indo-Pacific region through collaboration 
with major stakeholders, including ASEAN and Southeast Asian countries. 
The ROK’s Indo-Pacific Strategy presents a comprehensive economic and 
security framework. Given the ROK’s status as an Indo-Pacific nation, its core national 
interests are intricately linked to the stability and prosperity of the region. Within this 
framework, Korea aims to strengthen the rules-based international order and promote an 
inclusive multilateral system. 
One notable aspect of the ROK’s evolving foreign policy is the broadening 
geographical scope through its Indo-Pacific Strategy, which now encompasses 
Southeast Asia, South Asia, Oceania, and the African Coast of the Indian Ocean. This 
expansion seeks to establish a strategic partnership network tailored to the Indo-Pacific 
region’s unique needs and opportunities. 
The Indo-Pacific Strategy is anchored in three core principles: inclusiveness, trust,

The Belt and Road Initiative, A Pathway to Global 
Harmony and Prosperity 

The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has revitalized a rich history of cultural 
interactions spanning over two thousand years and ignited the aspirations of over 150 
nations to realize a shared vision: peace, harmony, and prosperity. 
Collaboration within the BRI framework has ushered in significant and deep-
seated transformations globally, marking an important milestone in the annals of human 
history. 
Despite some missteps, loopholes, and shortcomings, it is safe to argue that the 
BRI remains one of the world’s largest platforms for international cooperation. It is a 
driving force of re-globalization and forming a new world economic order. 
The third Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation, which is taking 
place in Beijing this week, presents an opportunity for deep reflections, honest 
assessment, and contemplation while setting directions for a new era. Cambodian Prime 
Minister Hun Manet will deliver an address at the Forum to share the Cambodian 
perspective on the BRI and the way forward. 
In a world beset by turbulence, complexity, uncertainty, and fragmentation, the 
BRI emerges as a beacon of hope, offering a vision for a brighter, more inclusive, 
cooperative future. 
The current global landscape is fraught with escalating rivalries among major 
powers, wars and conflicts, a sluggish global economic recovery, and a climate 
emergency. Zero-sum power politics, protectionism, and unilateralism are rising, 
threatening to undermine international cooperation. 
Humanity’s challenges today are unparalleled after the end of the Cold War. The 
deficit in peace, development, security, and governance is widening, posing a grave 
threat to humanity and the planet. 
From regional conflicts and arms races to food security, cyber-attacks, and climate 
change, these multifaceted challenges demand cooperation and a united response. 
We must seek innovative ideas and concepts for a just, equitable, and effective 
global governance system. The BRI offers an open and safe space for nations to 
innovate and unite in the pursuit of exchanges between civilizations. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 165 
Volume IV 
The BRI is not solely about China’s development but a solution for global 
development issues. It recognizes that economic globalization is an irreversible trend 
that must be made more open, inclusive, balanced, and beneficial. It seeks to advance 
modernization in participating countries, fostering dynamic, inclusive, and sustainable 
economic growth. 
The BRI envisions a global community of shared futures, as highlighted in the BRI 
White Paper. It transcends ideological differences and national borders, creating a 
platform for mutual trust, economic integration, and cultural inclusiveness. It offers a 
practical means to build a fairer and more equitable global governance system, guiding 
humanity towards a better future. 
The BRI is firmly grounded in the principles of extensive consultation, joint 
contribution, and shared benefits. It champions win-win cooperation and encourages 
economic integration, interconnected development, and the equitable sharing of 
achievements. It is an open, green, and clean initiative, ensuring that progress is both 
steady and high-quality. 
In line with the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the BRI promotes 
coordinated economic, social, and eco-environmental development. It addresses root 
causes and obstacles, striving for lasting, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth. 
Over the past decade, the BRI has yielded remarkable results, opening new 
avenues for global economic growth and improving people’s lives worldwide. The BRI 
remains committed to global connectivity and multilateralism in an era marked by de-
globalization. 
The BRI is a path to global well-being, peace, prosperity, openness, innovation, 
and social progress. It promotes all-round connectivity in various fields, facilitating policy 
coordination, infrastructure development, unimpeded trade, financial integration, and 
people-to-people ties. 
Cooperation in scientific and technological innovation accelerates, promoting 
technology transfer, knowledge sharing, and talent training. Digital Silk Road cooperation, 
for instance, fosters an open and equitable environment for digital development. 
The BRI supports trade and investment liberalization, eliminating barriers and 
enhancing global trade efficiency. Building synergies between the BRI and other regional 
initiatives, such as the ASEAN-led Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership 
(RCEP) would be essential. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 166 
Volume IV 
The BRI advocates for exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations, 
rejecting divisive concepts like the “clash of civilizations.” Instead, it promotes dialogue, 
inclusiveness, and shared values, uniting cultures and hearts across borders. 
The BRI represents a vast and enduring global project for the 21st century, 
marked by its long-term, cross-border, and systematic nature. Building upon the 
achievement over the past decade, the BRI will showcase increased innovation and 
dynamism, fostering greater openness and inclusivity, thereby creating new opportunities 
for all. 
Indeed, for the continued expansion of the BRI, it is imperative to emphasize 
principles of good governance, which encompass transparency, accountability, and 
quality. The Chinese government and private sectors must redouble their efforts to 
bolster good governance and combating corruption. 
It is challenging for China to convince other participating countries and partners 
that the BRI is not a geopolitical project but purely an economic and cultural project. 
Looking ahead, the BRI may encounter new challenges. Nevertheless, if all 
participating parties join forces, collaborate closely, and persevere, they can surmount 
these obstacles and elevate their collective efforts, shared contributions, and mutual 
benefits to new heights. Cooperation will flourish and shine in the dark, and the BRI can 
anticipate an even more promising future.

Unpacking the Conflict in the Middle East 

The complexity of conflict in the Middle East often gets oversimplified in public 
discourse. The region is frequently depicted as a battleground for a clash of civilizations 
or religious warfare. 
However, the underlying reality is more about geopolitical competition than 
ideological or theological differences. 
The Middle East’s unique geographical and strategic position has historically 
attracted the attention of major global powers seeking to further their interests in the 
area. This region is home to the largest oil reserves in the world, which has consistently 
drawn foreign involvement since the end of World War II. 
Additionally, the Middle East is vitally important as the origin and spiritual 
heartland of the three major monotheistic religions: Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. 
Its geopolitical significance means that any local or regional conflicts have the 
potential not just to disrupt the area’s own stability or alter its balance of power, but also 
to impact global stability. 
Consequently, the Middle East remains a crucial focal point in international affairs, 
playing a pivotal role economically, politically, and culturally. 
Great-power rivalry significantly shapes the Middle East’s geopolitical landscape. 
The interests of global powers like the United States, Russia, and China converge 
around regional centers of economic and political influence and countries that maintain 
historical relationships with these powers. 
This web of influences dictates much of the regional dynamics, including military 
alliances and enmities. 
In the intricate geopolitical chessboard that is the Middle East, the United States 
has long held the dominant position, particularly in military terms. However, this 
supremacy is no longer unchallenged as Russia and China increasingly assert their 
presence. 
Yet, the motivation behind these great powers’ involvement in potential future 
conflicts in the region extends beyond mere competition over expanding spheres of 
influence. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 168 
Volume IV 
The interconnection between counterterrorism efforts and great-power competition 
in the Middle East is becoming increasingly evident. As the U.S. recalibrates its 
engagement level in the region, it inadvertently sets the stage for other powers to step 
in, potentially through proxy conflicts. 
This dynamic illustrates a delicate balance where the extent of U.S. involvement 
can either deter or encourage other great powers’ deeper participation based on 
perceived opportunities or threats. 
Notably, the United States, China, and Russia show limited appetite for direct 
military confrontation in the Middle East unless their core interests face direct threats. 
This cautious approach suggests a strategic calculation that weighs the high risks of 
direct involvement against the geopolitical benefits of influence achieved through less 
overt means. 
Moreover, any conflicts involving these great powers in the Middle East today are 
unlikely to mirror the proxy wars of the Cold War era. The geopolitical landscape has 
dramatically evolved since then, with new technologies, changing political alliances, and 
a complex web of economic interdependencies reshaping traditional military 
engagements. 
Thus, while the specter of great-power competition looms large, the nature of 
conflict and engagement in the Middle East continues to evolve, driven by a confluence 
of strategic interests that transcend simple rivalry. 
This nuanced reality calls for a sophisticated understanding of the motives and 
constraints influencing U.S., Chinese, and Russian strategies in the region. As these 
powers navigate the turbulent waters of Middle Eastern politics, their actions are likely to 
be calculated, cautious, and, above all, aimed at balancing risk against the strategic 
advantage in an increasingly multipolar world order or a multiplex world. 
A poignant example of this is the evolving relationship between Israel and Iran. 
Once allies during the reign of Iran’s last Shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, their 
friendship ended abruptly with Iran’s 1979 Islamic Revolution. 
Iran’s new theocratic regime positioned itself staunchly against Israel, labeling it 
an imperialist entity in the region. This shift set the stage for decades of indirect conflicts. 
Iran has supported organizations like Hamas and the Hezbollah militia, which Israel and 
many Western nations consider terrorist groups. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 169 
Volume IV 
In response, Israel perceives Iran’s potential nuclear capabilities as a direct threat 
to its existence and has not hesitated to undertake covert operations to impede Iran’s 
nuclear ambitions. 
The Israeli military operations in the Gaza Strip, which results in a serious 
humanitarian disaster and a clear violation of the principles of humanitarian law, coupled 
with the escalating violence in the West Bank, significantly heighten regional tensions 
and amplify the risk of a broader conflict in the Middle East. 
The ongoing covert conflict between Israel and Iran, often referred to as a 
“shadow war,” highlights how longstanding rivalries and alliances in the Middle East are 
catalyzed by the strategic interests of global powers rather than solely by religious or 
cultural disputes. This shadow war has seen both nations engaging in acts of sabotage 
and proxy battles, reflecting a broader pattern of geopolitical maneuvering rather than 
isolated incidents of aggression. 
Hence, the strife in the Middle East is a tapestry of power struggles intricately 
linked to the interests of global superpowers. Understanding these dynamics is crucial 
for any meaningful analysis of the region’s enduring conflicts. Such an understanding 
shifts the narrative from one of inherent sectarian violence to a more accurate portrayal 
of strategic geopolitical competition.

China and the US Stabilizing their Complex Ties 

Accounting for over 40 percent of global GDP, the US-China relationship is 
undeniably the most significant and complex bilateral relationship in the world. 
The interactions between these two major powers not only shape their own 
futures but also have profound impacts on global stability, economic growth, and 
international security.

positive and constructive direction. Cooperation and competition are intertwined. 
Southeast Asian countries including Cambodia wish to see a healthy and stable US-
China competition. 
The visit of the US National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan to China last week 
underscored a mutual political commitment to stabilizing their complex relationship. The 
discussions were marked by a refreshing level of candor. 
China has repeatedly emphasized the importance of strategic perception, likening 
it to the “first button of a shirt” that must be correctly fastened. 
“Establishing the right perception is key for China and the United States to achieve 
peaceful coexistence,” noted Wang Yi, China’s top diplomat. 
The widening “trust deficit” between the world’s leading superpower and the 
largest developing country significantly heightens the risks associated with the Taiwan 
issue and other global challenges, including the tensions in the South China Sea, 
conflicts in Ukraine, the Middle East, and the Korean Peninsula. Addressing these 
challenges requires coordinated and concerted efforts from both sides. 
In a rare move, Jake Sullivan met with General Zhang Youxia, Vice-Chairman of 
China’s Central Military Commission, before his meeting with President Xi Jinping. This 
meeting, along with extensive discussions with Wang Yi, underscores the seriousness 
with which both sides are approaching the current state of affairs. 
During their talks, Wang and Sullivan explored the possibility of upcoming 
discussions between US President Joe Biden and President Xi. 
They exchanged contrasting views on key global issues, including the conflicts in 
the Middle East and Ukraine, China’s territorial claims in the South China Sea, Taiwan, 
and trade disputes. “The key to the smooth development of China-U.S. interaction lies in

treating each other as equals,” Wang emphasized, reflecting a core principle that China 
seeks to uphold in its dealings with the US. 
President Xi highlighted the need for global solidarity and coordination in a world 
marked by change and turbulence, rather than exclusion or regression. 
Sullivan conveyed President Biden’s commitment to managing the US-China 
relationship in a way that avoids conflict, expressing that Biden “looks forward to 
engaging with you in the coming weeks.” The White House characterized the discussions 
as “candid, substantive, and constructive.” 
Sullivan also advocated for improved military-to-military communication during his 
meeting with General Zhang, marking the first encounter between Zhang and an official 
from the Biden administration. 
He stressed the shared responsibility of both nations to prevent their competition 
from escalating into conflict. The progress in military communications and upcoming 
talks between theatre-level commanders were seen as critical steps toward stabilizing 
regional tensions. 
In addition, Sullivan reiterated the importance of maintaining stability across the 
Taiwan Strait and ensuring freedom of navigation in the South China Sea, a crucial trade 
route. He also raised concerns about China’s support for Russia’s defense industrial 
base amid the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

between Presidents Xi and Biden has been pivotal in steering the course of US-China 
relations. However, for these interactions to translate into a stable, healthy, and 
sustainable relationship, both nations must back their words with concrete actions. 
While communication is a positive development, it alone is insufficient. Beijing is 
ready to turn goodwill into tangible results, and the international community now awaits 
Washington’s demonstration of sincerity in managing differences and cooperating with 
China. 
Domestic politics in the US and anti-China sentiment have a substantial impact on 
the bilateral relationship between the US and China. The US has increasingly framed its 
policy towards China through a lens of competition and containment, driven by concerns 
about China’s rising global influence and its economic and military advancements.

support for regional partners and allies who are wary of China’s ambitions.

advanced technologies and critical supply chains. Additionally, there is significant

strategy.

ASEAN at a Crossroad 

This week, ASEAN leaders will gather in Vientiane for their annual Summits 
among themselves and with dialogue partners, under the theme “ASEAN: Enhancing 
Connectivity and Resilience.” 
The theme reflects the Lao PDR’s focus as ASEAN Chair on strengthening 
ASEAN’s integration across its three community pillars: the political-security community, 
the economic community, and the socio-cultural community. 
With a focus on infrastructure development, narrowing the development gap, 
fostering greater economic integration, and enhancing people-to-people exchanges, the 
Lao Chair aims to strengthen ASEAN’s agency to navigate uncertainties and complexities 
caused by heightening geostrategic competition, economic fragmentation, and the re-
emergence of bloc politics. 
The organization’s success or failure in addressing these challenges will 
determine not only its future relevance but also its ability to act as a stabilizing force in 
the broader Asia Pacific region. 
 ASEAN Connectivity 
Connectivity has long been viewed as a cornerstone of ASEAN’s integration 
process. The Master Plan on ASEAN Connectivity 2025 seeks to bridge infrastructure 
gaps, promote economic interdependence, and foster deeper socio-cultural ties among 
member states. This vision of connectivity is critical to transforming ASEAN from a 
collection of individual economies into a more cohesive, competitive regional bloc. 
However, while connectivity has brought benefits, it also presents challenges. As 
regional powers, particularly China and the United States, vie for influence in Southeast 
Asia, infrastructure projects—many of them tied to foreign investments—risk becoming 
battlegrounds for geostrategic rivalry. 
Thus, ASEAN’s connectivity strategy must be viewed through a dual lens: on the 
one hand, it serves as a mechanism for greater regional integration; on the other, it 
exposes member states to external influences, heightening the importance of collective 
decision-making and strategic foresight in managing these relationships. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 174 
Volume IV 
ASEAN must ensure that its connectivity projects are not driven solely by external 
powers’ interests but align with the region’s long-term vision for sustainable, inclusive 
development. 
 ASEAN Resilience 
Resilience is equally critical in a world characterized by fast-changing and 
unpredictable geopolitical and geo-economic landscapes. ASEAN must enhance its 
collective resilience to navigate the strategic uncertainties arising from intensifying 
competition between global powers. The ongoing US-China rivalry has far-reaching 
implications for Southeast Asia, threatening to polarize the region and challenge 
ASEAN’s long-held principle of neutrality and non-alignment. 
ASEAN’s ability to remain resilient amidst these challenges depends on 
strengthening its internal cohesion. The development of strategic plans for implementing 
the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 will be crucial in guiding the organization’s response 
to external pressures while promoting internal solidarity. 
However, ASEAN’s internal diversity—ranging from economic disparities to 
divergent political systems—makes this an uphill task. The risk is that divisions within 
ASEAN could undermine its ability to present a united front on critical issues. 
The world is transitioning toward a multipolar or multiplex global order, where 
power is no longer concentrated in a few dominant states but distributed across a 
broader spectrum of actors. 
ASEAN’s capacity to withstand the pressures of this shifting global order will 
depend largely on its ability to enhance resilience through greater cooperation, trust-
building, and proactive policymaking. 
 ASEAN Centrality 
At the heart of ASEAN’s identity is its commitment to maintaining centrality in the 
regional architecture. ASEAN centrality hinges on two key pillars: its convening power 
and its normative power. 
Convening power refers to ASEAN’s ability to bring together major global and 
regional actors in an inclusive setting—whether through the East Asia Summit (EAS), the 
ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), or the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus (ADMM-
Plus). ASEAN’s neutral platforms have, in the past, allowed it to mediate tensions and 
promote dialogue, especially in times of heightened geopolitical rivalry. 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 175 
Volume IV 
As major powers become more assertive in asserting their influence, ASEAN risks 
being sidelined in critical regional security discussions. To preserve its centrality, ASEAN 
must recalibrate its strategies and engage in more proactive, sometimes assertive, 
diplomacy, ensuring that its voice remains central in shaping the evolving regional 
architecture. 
ASEAN’s normative power, meanwhile, is grounded in its commitment to 
principles such as non-interference, peaceful dispute resolution, and consensus-building. 
The Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) and the ASEAN Charter are foundational to 
ASEAN’s normative framework. 
However, for these principles to remain relevant, ASEAN must ensure that they 
are actively upheld, both within its own membership and by external partners. Challenges 
to ASEAN’s normative influence have emerged, with some external actors disregarding 
the region’s norms in favor of unilateral actions. 
 The Path Forward: Ensuring ASEAN’s Relevance 
To ensure its relevance in this evolving geopolitical landscape, ASEAN must 
prioritize both internal unity and proactive engagement with external powers. The ASEAN 
Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP) is a promising initiative that promotes ASEAN’s 
centrality while addressing the geostrategic complexities of the Asia Pacific region. 
By focusing on practical cooperation in areas such as maritime security, 
sustainable development, and disaster resilience, the AOIP offers a framework for 
maintaining ASEAN’s central role without taking sides in great power competition. 
However, initiatives like the AOIP must be accompanied by concrete actions. 
ASEAN cannot afford to rest on its laurels. It must continuously refine and innovate its 
institutional mechanisms, strengthen its internal solidarity, and assert its normative 
influence in the face of rising external pressures. 
The resilience and relevance of ASEAN in this multipolar or multiplex world will 
depend on its ability to adapt to new realities, while staying true to its foundational 
principles of cooperation, openness, inclusivity, peaceful co-existence, non-interference, 
and respect for international law. 
As ASEAN convenes in Vientiane, it must seize this critical moment to 
demonstrate that it remains a key actor, not just in Southeast Asia but in the wider Asia 
Contemporary Perspective 
Part II: The Asia Pacific 
P a g e | 176 
Volume IV 
Pacific region. The path forward requires strategic foresight, unity, and the political will to 
assert ASEAN’s centrality in an increasingly fractured world.

The forum aims to foster a comprehensive understanding of AI governance within the Cambodian context, addressing key facets such as ethical considerations in the public sector, the intersection of data privacy and business innovation, regulatory landscapes that will shape AI development, and the societal impact of AI. In the initial segment of the forum, our distinguished keynote speakers focus on the ethical implementation of AI in both public and private sectors. Following that, in the subsequent section, our panelists will tackle the societal ramifications of AI and the importance of regulating AI to promote its beneficial impact on our society. The forum will bring together key stakeholders from academia, industry, and government officials to engage in meaningful discussions, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving.

Wherever your studies take you, with CamTech University you’ll find a supportive and dynamic home in Phnom Penh. Do you still remember CamTech Seminar Series? Committed to contributing to the development of Cambodia’s economy through the training of students in science and technology, CamTech will host the 2nd AI Seminar Series on a prominent question, “Will AI help or replace humans?” Due to technological advancement, AI has been made so smart that some researchers believe that AI is even smarter than humans. This sounds scary to some, while some others see this as an opportunity for us to mobilize AI to assist humans to achieve works not feasible by humans alone. The number of pros and cons of AI is so massive that it cannot be described in this short post alone. To feed your curiosity about AI, please come to attend our 2nd AI Seminar Series to be conducted on Thursday, 04th November 2021 from 5:30 to 7:00 PM via this Zoom link below. In today’s digital era, artificial intelligence (AI) presents itself as a powerful tool with both positive and negative implications. On one hand, AI streamlines tasks, offers personalized recommendations and enhances decision-making. On the other hand, it can perpetuate bias, compromise privacy, and potentially replace jobs, impacting the economy. It is crucial to approach AI development with care, considering its potential consequences. That’s why the upcoming CamTech Seminar AI Series 4 will focus on “Embracing compassionate AI”. Esteemed speakers will explore ethical AI usage, policy development, responsible AI development and deployment, and mindful education. Join us as we navigate the ethical dimensions of AI and strive for a compassionate and beneficial AI future.

---

In today’s digital era, Data plays a critical role in making informed business decisions. It allows businesses to identify trends and patterns, improve efficiency, use predictive analytics, measure success, gain customer insights, and manage risks effectively. By leveraging data, businesses can stay ahead of competitors and achieve their goals in an ever-changing marketplace. In this seminar, our distinguished speakers will delve into the use of data-driven decision making in both the global and Cambodia markets. Through various case studies, they will demonstrate how businesses across different sectors can leverage data to inform their strategic decisions. Additionally, our speakers will offer insights on how to improve one’s proficiency in data science. During the Fireside Chat session, our panelists will further discuss Cambodia’s level of readiness and ability to adopt data analytics tools and technology, which can help drive business growth and development.

## Faculty Of Arts, Humanities And Social Sciences

University students should not learn only content knowledge and skills, but they should also learn to become well-rounded citizens in society.

Art, Humanities and Social Sciences serve just these functions.

The faculty of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences offers 11 majors from four departments for students to choose from.

Vision & Missions

The Faculty of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences aspires to lead in education, teaching and learning, research and innovation in the area of arts, humanities, social science and technology and to passionate commitment to their profession as well as to social development.

- Encourage lecturers to provide high quality teaching, research-informed teaching, and applied high impact research and innovation, which also engages students.
- Seek and maintain innovative teaching and learning practices in order to become a role model for good educational practices.
- Transform our graduates with the mindset that encourages lifelong learning, integrity, creativity and innovation, and professionalism so that they can become leaders in the area of arts, humanities, social science and technology-enhanced learning;
- To serve as a focal point of intellectual and academic exchange to enable local, national, and international collaboration on teaching and research in the area of arts, humanities, social science and technology-enhanced learning

ក្នុងការថ្លែងងសន្ទរកថា បើកនៃសិន្នសិទ ឯកឧត្តម ហែម វណ្ណឌី រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីក្រសួងឧស្សាហកម្ម វិទ្យាសាស្ត្រ បច្ចេកវិទ្យា និងនវានុវត្តន៍បានលើកឡើងថា៖ “វាមិនមែនជារឿងដែលថា តើបច្ចេកវិទ្យាទាំងនេះនឹងកំណត់អនាគតរបស់យើង ឬអត់នោះទេ។ សំណួរពិតប្រាកដគឺថា តើយើងនឹងដឹកនាំការអភិវឌ្ឍបច្ចេកវិទ្យាទាំងនេះយ៉ាងណា ប្រកបដោយភាពឆ្លាតវៃ និងមានទំនួលខុសត្រូវ ដើម្បីបម្រើគោលដៅបង្កើនវឌ្ឍនភាពសម្រាប់មនុស្សជាតិ។”

ឯកឧត្តមបានលើកឡើងពីកិច្ចខិតខំប្រឹងប្រែងរបស់កម្ពុជា ក្នុងការពង្រឹងប្រព័ន្ធអេកូឡូស៊ីនវានុវត្តន៍ តាមរយៈផែនទីបង្ហាញផ្លូវវិទ្យាសាស្ត្រ បច្ចេកវិទ្យា និងនវានុវត្តន៍២០៣០ និងបានសង្កត់ធ្ងន់លើសារៈសំខាន់នៃការវិនិយោគលើមូលធនមនុស្ស និងសមត្ថភាពផ្នែក STEM ។

ឯកឧត្តមរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីបានបន្ថែមថា៖ “យើងត្រូវតម្រង់ទិសការវិនិយោគរបស់យើងកាន់តែស៊ីជម្រៅ លើការអភិវឌ្ឍមូលធនមនុស្ស។ សាកលវិទ្យាល័យមិនអាចធ្វើការងារនេះតែឯងបានទេ។ ដូច្នេះ កិច្ចសហការរវាងរដ្ឋាភិបាល វិស័យសិក្សាស្រាវជ្រាវ ឧស្សាហកម្ម និងដៃគូក្នុងតំបន់ពិតជាចាំបាច់។” ក្នុងនោះផងដែរ លោកបណ្ឌិត Ko Young-Joo ប្រធានសហគមន៍នវានុវត្តន៍ និងគោលនយោបាយអាស៊ី បានបង្ហាញការប្តេជ្ញាចិត្តផ្នែកសង្គមរបស់សហគមន៍នេះ ក្នុងការជំរុញការស្រាវជ្រាវដែលមានគុណភាពខ្ពស់ និងការបណ្តុះគំនិតច្នៃប្រឌិតនៅទូទាំងតំបន់។

ឯកឧត្តមរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីបានបន្ថែមថា៖ “យើងត្រូវតម្រង់ទិសការវិនិយោគរបស់យើងកាន់តែស៊ីជម្រៅ លើការអភិវឌ្ឍមូលធនមនុស្ស។ សាកលវិទ្យាល័យមិនអាចធ្វើការងារនេះតែឯងបានទេ។ ដូច្នេះ កិច្ចសហការរវាងរដ្ឋាភិបាល វិស័យសិក្សាស្រាវជ្រាវ ឧស្សាហកម្ម និងដៃគូក្នុងតំបន់ពិតជាចាំបាច់។” ក្នុងនោះផងដែរ លោកបណ្ឌិត Ko Young-Joo ប្រធានសហគមន៍នវានុវត្តន៍ និងគោលនយោបាយអាស៊ី បានបង្ហាញការប្តេជ្ញាចិត្តផ្នែកសង្គមរបស់សហគមន៍នេះ ក្នុងការជំរុញការស្រាវជ្រាវដែលមានគុណភាពខ្ពស់ និងការបណ្តុះគំនិតច្នៃប្រឌិតនៅទូទាំងតំបន់។

On Thursday, 23 December 2021, CamTech University was honored to receive a visit from Her Excellency Koung Sorita, Under-Secretary of State of Ministry of Women’s Affairs (MOWA), and Mrs. Chea Sokheak, CEO of Sorya Center Point. The campus visit is initiated with the purpose of introducing CamTech University to the Ministry of Women’s Affairs and exchanging ideas in order to explore possible areas of collaboration. CamTech University and MOWA acknowledged that current labor supplies have failed to catch up with the growing demand for skilled labor from the industries as Cambodia is transitioning to Digital Economy and Industry 4.0.

It is worth highlighting that CamTech’s goals and vision align well with those of MOWA since we both are striving to promote STEAM education, entrepreneurship, and woman empowerment. CamTech University is dedicated to building more partnerships with relevant Ministry, Industry and Community to provide high-quality education and equip our students with pertinent skills and knowledge.

Professor Rethy’s speech about his life journey to becoming a scientist has inspired all the CamTech students to pursue their dreams and do what they believe is right for themselves. “I have no regrets in my life because I do what I want to do,” the professor responded to one of the students’ inquiry. These remarks have enabled the students to perceive their own potential.

As long as you hold an unwavering passion or potential for a particular endeavor, nothing is impossible in life.

To promote the Triple Helix Model, the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) and the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology, and Innovation (MISTI) co-hosted a multidisciplinary and multi-stakeholder consultation workshop on “Cambodia National Technology Roadmap for Education 2021 – 2030: Enhancing Education with Technology” On December 01, 2021 with support from the Science and Technology Policy Institute (STEPI) of South Korea. The consultation workshop was participated by relevant stakeholders from various backgrounds and representatives from EdTech Committee, the National Council for Science, Technology, and Innovation, research institutes, universities, private sectors, practitioners, school leadership, government officials, and students. The purpose of the workshop was to identify and gather input for vision, goals, strategic products and services, and key advanced technologies to support the diffusion of technology in the Cambodian educational sector.

Four areas of educational technology, namely The Essentials, Management System, Enhancing Apparatus, and Capacity Building have been identified as the pillar of focus. Additionally, all stakeholders have come to an agreement that active collaboration among universities, industry, and government is of great significance in steering the development and implementation of the national roadmap to achieve desirable outcomes. It is CamTech’s privilege to undertake this prestigious task to develop the Cambodia National Technology Roadmap and contribute to the ongoing efforts in promoting education innovation in the country.

CamTech and E-GetS Sign MOU on Strategic Partnership

On the morning of November 19, the signing ceremony for a memorandum of understanding (hereinafter MOU) between Cambodia University of Technology and Science and E-GetS was held in Phnom Penh. CamTech President Prof. Dr. Khieng Sothy, Associate Vice President for Business Development Ms. Lilian Li, E-GetS Vice Presidents Mr. Zhang Juhui and Ms. Wang Huifang, student and teacher representatives, as well as local and international media attended the event. The ceremony marks the prologue of collaboration to advance the integration of higher education and the digital technology industry in Cambodia.

The workshop was held on the afternoon of June 30, 2022, with the participation of 44 teachers and students. In this workshop, CamTech students also shared their learning experiences and presented various projects such as AR / VR Games to the students at Sovannaphumi School.

During the event, Ms. Lilian Li outlined key initiatives under the MOU. As part of the collaboration, CamTech and E-GetS will jointly establish an employment training and internship base, designed to bridge academic knowledge with cutting-edge industry practice. Furthermore, E-GetS will offer USD 100,000 to CamTech’s scholarship fund for talent development and targeted training. Ms. Li praised E-GetS’s support and highlighted that these efforts will equip students with more profound professional experience, fostering new talent for Cambodia’s digital transformation.

In his address, Mr. Zhang Juhui gave a detailed introduction to E-GetS’s development history, business scope, and corporate culture. He emphasized that the company will leverage its technological and platform strengths to collaborate with CamTech in operating the training base, offering students practical opportunities, scholarships, and specialized training programs. The partnership aims to cultivate versatile talent for the digital economy and drive Cambodia’s digital transformation.

Following the speeches, senior representatives from CamTech and E-GetS signed the MOU and officially established their partnership. As a symbol of the cooperation’s transition into action, CamTech presented E-GetS the honorary “Employment Training and Internship Base” plaque, while E-GetS provided a USD 100,000 scholarship for the university.

The World Economic Forum reported that skills, such as complex problem solving, critical thinking, creativity, will become highly sought after and necessary to thrive in Industry 4.0. Therefore, the task of education institutions is to develop an innovative curriculum which responds to the demands of Industry 4.0. However, this responsibility cannot fall solely on a single institution. In fact, no single institution will be able to address the challenges of Industry 4.0. The issue of skills affects multiple stakeholders. Hence, various institutions must contribute to this nation-wide effort. Education institutions must provide a holistic education, so that students will become well-rounded, responsible citizens with the necessary hard and soft skills to prosper in this dynamic world. Furthermore, it is the responsibility of industries to work closely with education institutions to co-develop a curriculum which reflect the needs, demands and technological trends in the labor market. Additionally, companies should provide internship opportunities and industry placements for students, so that they can link concepts and theories in the classroom with the world of work.

## CamTech University Press

CamTech University Press is an academic publishing platform that facilitates the publication of articles in peer-reviewed journals, with a primary focus on Science, Technology, and Sustainability (STS). It is dedicated to exploring the interplay of science and technology within the context of sustainability, adopting an interdisciplinary approach that incorporates perspectives from history, economics, political science, international relations, science policy, innovation, technology management, governance, and environmental studies. The press aims to advance scholarly research and discourse in these areas, promoting rigorous, peer-reviewed contributions that address the challenges and opportunities of sustainable development through science and technology.

On the 22nd of October 2021, CamTech University and Drone Khmer Technology (DKT) Co. Ltd signed an MoU to launch a new knowledge transfer project for drone technology. This is, so far, the first university-industry knowledge transfer project in Cambodia. The project aims to develop a digitally transformed AI-Powered business management and decision support system to enhance efficiency, increase productivity, and reduce the operational cost of DKT, and thus in turn, rural farmers for drone technology. This MoU shall include data collection, data analysis for decision making, training to the customers/stakeholders, replacement/repair/maintenance of drones, and helping to enhance capabilities across all business functions. With a target for a 3-year project, DKT shall provide funds, donate a drone for the CamTech University lab and offer training to the students. Professor Alamgir Hossain (Vice President and Professor of AI) will lead this project under his AI-Powered Village lab at CamTech University. CamTech University has reaffirmed its commitment to advancing Cambodia’s research capability and innovation ecosystem by becoming a founding member of the Cambodia Research Network (CRN), a national consortium that brings together 31 leading research-oriented universities and research institutions to strengthen evidence-based research, policy engagement, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

The University’s participation reflects its long-term strategy to cultivate a vibrant research culture, develop the next generation of researchers and innovators, and translate scientific knowledge into practical solutions that address Cambodia’s development priorities. As Cambodia’s leading technology-focused university, CamTech views research not only as an academic pursuit but also as a driver of innovation, industry collaboration, and national competitiveness.

The Cambodia Research Network was formally launched on 22 July 2026 through a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Economic, Social and Cultural Council (EcoSoc) under the Office of the Council of Ministers and 31 research-oriented universities and research institutions. The signing ceremony was presided over by His Excellency Vongsey Vissoth, Permanent Deputy Prime Minister and Minister in Charge of the Office of the Council of Ministers.

During the ceremony, His Excellency underscored the profound impact of global megatrends and artificial intelligence on Cambodia’s future, stressing that evidence-based research is essential for building national resilience, informing public policy, and supporting the implementation of the Royal Government’s Pentagonal Strategy. He described the Cambodia Research Network as the beginning of a new chapter in mobilising Cambodia’s intellectual community to contribute to national development.

CamTech has invested strategically in building research capacity through the establishment of its international graduate programme in Science, Technology and Innovation. The University also hosts the Comparative Education Society of Cambodia (CESCam), the Centre for Buddhist AI Ethics, the China–ASEAN Studies Centre, and the AI Forum, which foster interdisciplinary research and dialogue on emerging issues of national, regional, and global significance.

Complementing these initiatives, CamTech University Press promotes the dissemination of scholarly research and facilitates knowledge exchange among academics, industry, policymakers, and international partners. Together, these initiatives strengthen Cambodia’s research capability while advancing applied research, technological innovation, and evidence-based solutions.

Through its participation in the Cambodia Research Network, CamTech University looks forward to expanding research collaboration with government, academia, industry, and international partners, contributing expertise that accelerates innovation and supports Cambodia’s sustainable socio-economic development.

## Program Overview

The objective of this cybersecurity major is to equip students with skills that are relevant in this era of digital transformation. The increasing prevalence of digitization in all fields has made cybersecurity imperative for ensuring the security of data from all angles. The major curriculum has been meticulously crafted to impart lifelong learning, covering crucial facets of cybersecurity, such as software design and development, privacy and data security, cyber-network security, and ethical considerations of digital law. The program focuses on project-based learning, enabling students to acquire practical experience relevant to the industry. Through collaborative teamwork and the latest tools and technologies, students will gain hands-on experience, developing critical skills such as communication, problem-solving, and teamwork that are indispensable in a professional setting. Furthermore, an industry placement program lasting a year supplements the university’s hands-on approach by providing an opportunity for students to gain real-world work experience. ### Bachelor of Architecture

Technology, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), has been dominating every aspect of our built environment. CamTech’s Architecture Program is designed to equip students with the skills to use technology ethically, and its core is the smart Design Studio, which encourages students to have an in-depth understanding of building structures and critical issues in architectural design. Students will be able to immerse themselves in new, cutting-edge technology in construction and produce more sustainable buildings locally and internationally. We empower students to use new digital architecture technology such as AI, data analysis, 3D modeling for design, virtual reality, and so on to enable optimal design, sustainable architecture, energy efficiency, a safe environment, and time-saving. ### Bachelor of Interior Design

Interior Design at CamTech University focuses on the creation of innovative and exciting, lively interior spaces through the adaptation and spatial arrangement of buildings. Digital technologies such as augmented and virtual reality (AR & VR) will be utilized to make interior spaces more intuitive in the real world before they are constructed. ## Dr. Myo Oo

Dr. Myo Oo joined CamTech University in 2023 as a Research Associate and Lecturer. He holds an M.A. degree in History from Yangon University in Myanmar, as well as an additional M.A. degree and a Ph.D. degree in Language and Society from Hitotsubashi University in Japan. Prior to joining CamTech University, Dr. Oo served as an Assistant Director at the Department of Historical Research in Myanmar. He also worked as a Research Professor at the Institute for Southeast Asian Studies at Busan University of Foreign Studies (BUFS) in South Korea. He taught at the School of Southeast Asia at BUFS as an Assistant Professor. Dr. Oo’s research interests primarily lie in the field of Southeast Asian history, culture, and society. He has contributed to numerous research articles in research journals and peer-reviewed publications across Asia. Moreover, he has undertaken the translation of three volumes of a unique Burmese diary that provide insights into the socio-economic condition of the early colonial period in the 19th-century.

Dr. Seet Ai Mee former Minister of State for Education, Singapore (1988-1991) come to visit CamTech

On the morning of July 29, 2022, CamTech University welcomed Dr Seet Ai Mee, former Minister of State for Education, Singapore (1988-1991), currently the Founder and Chairman of E2STEM. Dr. Seet Ai Mee expressed her pleasure to visit CamTech.

In addition, Dr. Seet Ai Mee also met with former students of E2STEM School, who are students who have received full scholarships to study for 4 years at CamTech University. Dr. Seet Ai Mee revealed that all three of them are outstanding alumni of E2STEM. Currently, they are freshmen at CamTech university.

1. Mr. Line Regene, majoring in Cyber Security

2. Mr. Ung Chhoungchhav, majoring in Cyber Security

3. Mr. Ho Chanponleusophea, majoring in Robotics and Automation Engineering

Dr. Seet Ai Mee expressed a strong interest in the university, which has a good physical infrastructure and curriculum that responds to the 21st-century learning environment.

Member

Dr. Khieng, founding President of Cambodia University of Technology and Science and advisor to the National Council of Science, Technology, and Innovation, is an accomplished scholar, educator, and higher education administrator.

Previously, he served as Vice President (Research and Administration) at Kirirom Institute of Technology and spent a decade at Cambodia’s leading research think tank, the Cambodia Development Resource Institute (CDRI).

At CDRI, Dr. Khieng co-founded and led the Education Unit, co-edited several books on Cambodian education and science and technology, and authored the book The Dawn of Social Enterprise in Cambodia, based on his doctoral research. His interdisciplinary research interests include post-secondary education, social entrepreneurship and innovation, and science and technology. Dr. Khieng has held research fellowships at Griffith University and the University of Melbourne (Australia), and the Swiss Federal university for Vocational Education and Training. He is a co-founder and President of the Comparative Education Society of Cambodia (CESCam) and serves on the boards of CESCam and Compare: A Journal of Comparative and International Education (UK).

# Educational Technology Program Overview

December 6, 2023 2024-09-06 10:21
## Educational Technology Program Overview

## Program Overview

A Bachelor’s Degree in Educational Technology focuses on the intersection of technology and education to prepare students to integrate technology into educational settings through technology-enhanced teaching and learning processes. The program provides a strong foundation in education theory, instructional design, and technology implementation. Throughout the program, students will learn how to create and implement technology-based instructional materials, including multimedia presentations, online courses, and interactive games. They will also gain knowledge of emerging technologies such as virtual reality, artificial intelligence, and social media, and explore their potential technological applications in education. In addition, students will have opportunities to complete their internships or practicums in schools or other educational settings to gain hands-on experience in working with technology in education. Graduates of this program are equipped with critical thinking and problem-solving skills necessary to analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of technological tools and strategies in education.

## Program Learning Outcomes

- Demonstrate a deep understanding of various learning theories and design effective technology-based learning materials including multimedia-based instructional materials, online courses, interactive simulations, and games.

- Create, integrate, implement, and evaluate technology-based learning solutions in educational settings through various educational contexts to enhance learning outcomes.

- Evaluate and assess technology-based learning solutions, including conducting formative and summative evaluations, using data-driven insights to refine and improve these solutions.

- Work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders, including educators, designers, developers, and administrators to create effective technology-based learning solutions.

- Familiarize with professional ethics and standards related to educational technology, including issues such as privacy, data security, and accessibility.

- Familiarize with research methods and apply them to investigate and address issues related to the design, development, and implementation of technology-based learning solutions.

## Program Structure

The 4-year Bachelor’s Degree program contains 156 credits combining from 106 credits of coursework, 48 credits of internship and 2 credits of Industrial Placement Report. The courses are divided into three categories, including Common Courses, Specialized Courses, and Elective Courses.

## Center for Social Innovation

CamTech’s Center for Social Innovation promotes innovative solutions to address the challenges related to the Sustainable Development Goals and carries out activities that bring about “Society 5.0”, which is sustainable, circular, and people-centered.

Globally, digital transformation and rapid economic development have hugely influenced people’s daily lives, but they also put social healthiness at a critical tipping point. The growing mental health crisis and increasing plastic waste concern are a few examples of social problems we have faced. And it is almost certain that the crises will be even more severe over the next few decades, undermining the universal goals for sustainability.

To contribute to solving such challenges, CamTech’s Center for Social Innovation conducts research related to social innovation, participates in building a social economy ecosystem, and carries out activities that encourage an innovative and entrepreneurial way of thinking to achieve social impact and drive a positive societal transformation that will benefit everyone. We work with people and organizations, especially marginalized individuals, non-profit institutions, and social enterprises. We also support new models of doing business, new solutions, and new enterprises that contribute to Society 5.0. Our current activities include

- Nurture and grow startups and virtual businesses that promote sustainability and social economy
- Manage industrial placement
- Provide co-working space and resources
- Link CamTech to industries, academia, and government to build an ecosystem
- Incubate (social) enterprises

CamTech is a private, not-for-profit university established in 2021 with a mission to offer applied research and innovation-focused education to transform lives that respond to industrial development and socio-economic growth needs. Recognizing the importance of long-term financial stability and sustainability, the university has established the CamTech Endowment Fund to ensure its ability to fulfill its mission and provide exceptional educational opportunities for generations to come.

The purpose of the CamTech Endowment Fund is to provide a permanent source of income to support the university’s core mission and strategic priorities. This includes, but is not limited to:

• **Financial aid**: Providing scholarships and other financial assistance to deserving students.

• **Academic programs**: Supporting the development and enhancement of academic programs, faculty research, and educational resources.

• **Infrastructure development**: Funding for renovations, equipment upgrades, and new facilities (including student dormitory) to maintain a modern and conducive learning environment.

The CamTech Endowment Fund will be managed by a professional investment committee composed of individuals with expertise in financial management and investment strategies. The committee will develop and implement an investment strategy that aims to:

• **Generate sustainable income**: The investment portfolio will be diversified across different asset classes, such as equities, bonds, real estate, and alternative investments, to balance risk and potential return. This diversification will help to mitigate the impact of market volatility and provide a steady stream of income for the university.

• **Preserve the principal**: The committee will also prioritize the long-term preservation of the principal amount of the endowment fund. This is achieved by ensuring a portion of the portfolio 

is invested in assets with lower risk profiles, even if they offer lower returns.

• **Meet spending needs**: The committee will establish a sustainable spending policy that determines the annual distribution amount from the endowment fund. This amount will be based on a rolling average of the market value of the fund to ensure long-term sustainability and avoid depleting the principal.
