## Entry requirements & Visa

## Cambodia Student Visa Procedure

### Visa Category: E-class (ES) Student Visa

Foreign students enrolled in Cambodian educational institutions must obtain an E-class (ordinary) Student Visa, often referred to as ES. This visa permits legal study and residence in Cambodia, with options for multiple extensions while the course is ongoing.

### Duration & Extensions

- **Initial validity:** 30 days (Apply for tourist E-visa)
- **Extension options:** Inside Cambodia, you can extend it in increments of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months, depending on your study duration.

### Application Requirements for Initial Visa

Applicants should prepare and submit the following:

- Valid passport (min. 6 months validity).
- Passport-sized photos. (White Background)
- Letter of acceptance from CamTech or equivalent institution.
- Proof of financial capability to support living and tuition.
- Medical insurance documentation.

### How to Apply

- Visit the official eVisa website for Cambodia.
- Click on "Apply for eVisa" and select "Tourism (ordinary)" as the purpose of your visit.
- Fill out the application form with your personal information and upload the required documents, including your passport and a passport-style photo.
- Pay the visa fee online using a credit card or PayPal.
- Submit your application and wait for the approval notification via email.
- Print out your eVisa and bring it with you to Cambodia along with your passport and other supporting documents.

### Cost & Processing

- **Online visa (e-Visa):** USD $35, valid for 30 days, single-entry, processed in ~3 business days.
- **In-country visa extensions (ES):** additional fees apply—amounts may vary, but typical extension processing is through immigration services.

## History

# History

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education.

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education. The university was named the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) and receives support from the Federation of Khmer-Chinese in Cambodia with an *aim to cultivate Cambodian young professional talents in science and technology and enhance Cambodia’s economic development*, with technical partnership with established and reputable universities in the Asian region. In return, CamTech will equip their students with academic and hands-on training, which will increase their employability and contribute to the development of Cambodia.

*During the meeting  with  the Founder and the  Representative  of  Tianjin University of Technology, HE Dr* *Hang Chuon Naron**, the* *Minister of Education, Youth and Sport**, expressed his full support to the project of CamTech University.*

In March 2021, **CamTech** received the official approval from the Royal Government of Cambodia to operate with the establishment of five faculties: the Faculty of Engineering, the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, the Faculty of Business and Management, the Faculty of Applied Sciences, and the Faculty of Sustainable Built Environment. 

**Not-profit Status**The University is a private not-for-profit institution with the mission of enabling young bright students from different backgrounds to be equipped with quality education and practical skills to contribute to the development of Cambodia. The University can pursue income-generating activities, as long as any surplus is reinvested back into the University, to ensure quality and sustainability.

**Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Se Foundation**To contribute to the establishment of the university, Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Foundation (the Foundation) was founded. The Foundation has provided 5 hectares of land in Chroy Changva Satellite city as the campus of the CamTech University, and invested more than $3 million to build the campus with the main university building, state-of-the-art facilities, a garden and a canteen.

## J7 HERITAGE SCIENCE LAB

## J7 Heritage Science Lab (J7 Lab)

J7 Heritage Science Lab (J7 Lab) was founded to promotes cross-disciplinary research that encompasses interpretation, conservation and preservation of cultural heritage aspects through the integration of natural science, social sciences and the humanities. The vision and mission of J7 Lab is not only to conduct research related to heritage and archaeological science but also to act as a platform for scientific collaboration to protect Cambodian cultural heritage in general, that of King Jayavarman the Seventh in particular. In other words, J7 Lab intends to bring together a diversity of scientists in a combined effort to preserve and conserve Cambodian cultural heritage.

**Objectives**

1. To use scientific methods and technological tools to study and protect cultural heritage;
2. To develop testing methods that minimize the destruction of historic artifacts;
3. To collaborate with social scientists, humanities scholars and archaeologists;
4. To generate scientific evidence to inform public policy on cultural heritage management;
5. To foster public engagement with both science and cultural heritage.

**Deliverables**

- Advancing public understanding of Heritage Science’s roles in the protection of Angkor;
- Fostering cultural pride in youth, while inspiring them to pursue STEM careers;
- Producing high quality scientific publications and to advance heritage science, both from the academic and policy perspectives.

X-Ray Diffraction (XRD)

Trinocular Optical Polarizing Microscope

Magnetometer

Conventional Radiography

# Alamgir Hossain

August 16, 2021 2023-07-21 13:33
## Alamgir Hossain

###### Dr. Alamgir Hossain

Visiting Professor,

Professor of Artificial Intelligence

Professor Alamgir Hossain received his PhD degree from the Department of Automatic Control & Systems Engineering, University of Sheffield, UK. He is currently serving as the Professor of Artificial Intelligence and Lead of the Centre for Digital Innovation at Teesside University (TU). Prior to this, he also served at Anglia Ruskin University (as the Director of the IT Research Institute), Head of Digital Research and Innovation of the National Horizon Centre (TU), University of Northumbria at Newcastle (as head of Computational Intelligence Group), University of Bradford, University of Sheffield, Sheffield Hallam University and the University of Dhaka (as the head of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering). He has extensive research experience in artificial intelligence, medical informatics, big data analysis, mobile enabled expert systems, cyber security, real-time algorithm design, decision support systems, robotics and adaptive active noise and vibration control systems. Professor Hossain has led many large EU funded projects as an international lead/co-investigator, worth over £16 million. With a publication in Nature, he has published over 300 refereed research articles, contributed in 12 books, received the “F C Williams 1996” award for an IET journal (UK) and ‘Best Paper Awards’ for five conference articles. See further details of articles and citations in his Google Scholar account.

To promote the Triple Helix Model, the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) and the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology, and Innovation (MISTI) co-hosted a multidisciplinary and multi-stakeholder consultation workshop on “Cambodia National Technology Roadmap for Education 2021 – 2030: Enhancing Education with Technology” On December 01, 2021 with support from the Science and Technology Policy Institute (STEPI) of South Korea. The consultation workshop was participated by relevant stakeholders from various backgrounds and representatives from EdTech Committee, the National Council for Science, Technology, and Innovation, research institutes, universities, private sectors, practitioners, school leadership, government officials, and students. The purpose of the workshop was to identify and gather input for vision, goals, strategic products and services, and key advanced technologies to support the diffusion of technology in the Cambodian educational sector.

Four areas of educational technology, namely The Essentials, Management System, Enhancing Apparatus, and Capacity Building have been identified as the pillar of focus. Additionally, all stakeholders have come to an agreement that active collaboration among universities, industry, and government is of great significance in steering the development and implementation of the national roadmap to achieve desirable outcomes. It is CamTech’s privilege to undertake this prestigious task to develop the Cambodia National Technology Roadmap and contribute to the ongoing efforts in promoting education innovation in the country.

CamTech cares about professional development of our faculty members and staff and thus provides regular training sessions. On Saturday 11th December 2021, CamTech had great honor that Prof. Heidi Dahles of Griffith University and University Tasmania gave us a talk on “Writing for Publication”. For young researchers, it is necessary to understand what should be done in order to get their research papers published, especially in high impact journals. There were some key messages that the presentation conveyed. First, a good researcher must be also a good reader. Reading will provide researchers with ideas to write about. Second, your research should contribute to the existing knowledge, and thus it should propose to fill a gap or gaps in the literature. Third, a good researcher is also a good collaborator. Research is a tiring job and time consuming, so a researcher should find a partner or partners to share responsibility. Another benefit from collaboration is the contribution from experts from different fields, which are very beneficial for producing a well-rounded research work for publication. These three messages aforementioned are only examples of good practices for writing for publication, while in fact, there are many other factors to consider when one takes up a research project and aim to write for publication. Learning from peers and one’s own experience is vitally important for personal growth in any areas, including research and writing for publication.

# History

## History

# History

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education.

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education. The university was named the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) and receives support from the Federation of Khmer-Chinese in Cambodia with an *aim to cultivate Cambodian young professional talents in science and technology and enhance Cambodia’s economic development*, with technical partnership with established and reputable universities in the Asian region. In return, CamTech will equip their students with academic and hands-on training, which will increase their employability and contribute to the development of Cambodia.

*During the meeting  with  the Founder and the  Representative  of  Tianjin University of Technology, HE Dr* *Hang Chuon Naron**, the* *Minister of Education, Youth and Sport**, expressed his full support to the project of CamTech University.*

In March 2021, **CamTech** received the official approval from the Royal Government of Cambodia to operate with the establishment of five faculties: the Faculty of Engineering, the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, the Faculty of Business and Management, the Faculty of Applied Sciences, and the Faculty of Sustainable Built Environment. 

**Not-profit Status**The University is a private not-for-profit institution with the mission of enabling young bright students from different backgrounds to be equipped with quality education and practical skills to contribute to the development of Cambodia. The University can pursue income-generating activities, as long as any surplus is reinvested back into the University, to ensure quality and sustainability.

**Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Se Foundation**To contribute to the establishment of the university, Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Foundation (the Foundation) was founded. The Foundation has provided 5 hectares of land in Chroy Changva Satellite city as the campus of the CamTech University, and invested more than $3 million to build the campus with the main university building, state-of-the-art facilities, a garden and a canteen.

## Comparative Education Society Of Cambodia

## Comparative Education Society Of Cambodia

Comparative Education Society of Cambodia (CESCam) was established in 2018 by a group of prominent researchers in the field of educational research, but it was not until 2021 that CESCam’s permanent secretariat has been established at CamTech as a focal point for communication and logistics following a board of director’s meeting. Currently, CamTech’s president Dr. Khieng Sothy is also the elected-president of CESCam.

Overall vision of CESCam is to promote comparative education in Cambodia through fostering teaching and research in the area of comparative education, producing publication about Cambodian education and beyond, contributing to advancing philosophy, methodology and methods, and establishing networks with local and international research and educational institutions and other counterpart societies.

CamTech shares a similar vision as CESCam, and the former intends to stimulate intellectual environment and contribute with out-of-the-box thinking and detail-oriented research studies to address key issues in the Cambodian educational system. Our areas of research include:

- Economics of education
- Innovative and emerging models of education
- Digital education
- STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics) education
- Research culture and practice in higher education institutions
- Internationalization of higher education
- University-Industry partnership

One of the video series of “Message from President” In this video, Dr. Sothy Khieng, president of CamTech, highlighted how important STEM education is for the future of Cambodia and its people. STEM, an acronym that refers to science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, mainly is a field of study and a career path related to industry 4.0, digitalization, and the use of information technology. From his extensive experience across the globe from the USA, Europe, and Asia, Dr. Sothy Khieng concluded that to maintain a prosperous future for Cambodia and its economic growth, Cambodia’s younger generation needs to shift from low-skill careers to technology-oriented careers, in short, STEM careers. A publication in 2016 by Saint Blanquat & Associates, Co., Ltd. funded by the British Embassy in Phnom Penh lists the top 20 careers in Cambodia over the next 10 years, which include production line supervisors, automation technicians, architects, civil engineers, construction site supervisors, health and safety engineers, construction project managers, water supply experts, water sanitation experts, quality assurance specialists, chemists, public health analysts, doctors (general practitioners), medical laboratory technicians, psychologists, economists, actuaries, financial analysts, mechanics, network analysts, and software programmers.

# J7 Heritage Science Lab

## J7 Heritage Science Lab

## J7 Heritage Science Lab (J7 Lab)

J7 Heritage Science Lab (J7 Lab) was founded to promotes cross-disciplinary research that encompasses interpretation, conservation and preservation of cultural heritage aspects through the integration of natural science, social sciences and the humanities. The vision and mission of J7 Lab is not only to conduct research related to heritage and archaeological science but also to act as a platform for scientific collaboration to protect Cambodian cultural heritage in general, that of King Jayavarman the Seventh in particular. In other words, J7 Lab intends to bring together a diversity of scientists in a combined effort to preserve and conserve Cambodian cultural heritage.

**Objectives**

1. To use scientific methods and technological tools to study and protect cultural heritage;
2. To develop testing methods that minimize the destruction of historic artifacts;
3. To collaborate with social scientists, humanities scholars and archaeologists;
4. To generate scientific evidence to inform public policy on cultural heritage management;
5. To foster public engagement with both science and cultural heritage.

**Deliverables**

- Advancing public understanding of Heritage Science’s roles in the protection of Angkor;
- Fostering cultural pride in youth, while inspiring them to pursue STEM careers;
- Producing high quality scientific publications and to advance heritage science, both from the academic and policy perspectives.

**Technology**

X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF)

X-Ray Diffraction (XRD)

Trinocular Optical Polarizing Microscope

Magnetometer 

Magnetic Susceptibility Meter

Computed Tomography

Conventional Radiography

3D Imaging Lab

Survey Drone

J7 Lab is currently undertaking J7 Heritage Science Project with Professor. Dr. CHHEM Rethy, CamTech’s Permanent Vice Chairman of the Board of Trustees, as the project leader.

To respond to educational disruption caused by the COVID-19 Pandemic, CamTech has prepared the knowledge sharing session to provide insight on how to study online effectively and keep oneself mentally healthy. The sharing session is part of our policies to assist high school as well as university students to stay in good health physically and mentally during the pandemic. We believe that the sharing session will contribute to help students focus and perform well on their study.

The first sharing session was delivered on August 19, 2021 for the Tribal Education Group by Dr. CHEA Vatana, Director of the Center for Professional Education and Training. The Cambodia University of Technology and Science would like to sincerely thank the Tribal Education Group for their coordination.

On Friday, December 17th, 2021, H.E. Dr. Khieng Sothy, representing CamTech University, signed a Tri-Party MOU with Smart Axiata, represented by Mr. Feiruz Ikhwan, acting CEO of Smart Axiata, and Impact Hub Phnom Penh (Cambodia) Co. Ltd., represented by Mrs. Melanie Mossard, CEO of Impact Hub Phnom Penh, regarding an online entrepreneur platform using the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform Program. The signing event had honorable presents from H.E. Dr. Hang Chuon Narong, Minister of Education, and H.E. Vandeth Chea, Minister of Post and Telecommunications. CamTech is a private, non-profit, and research-incentive university among ten leading public and private universities that signed this MOU. Two of our senior lecturers had completed entrepreneurship training using the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform prior to this event. CamTech will use the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform as part of entrepreneurship courses as well as in our Social Innovation Center (SCI).

The SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform is an educational initiative between Impact Hub Phnom Penh and Smart Axiata Co., Ltd. It is the first local online learning platform that introduces entrepreneurship through a blended learning approach to Cambodian students in Khmer and English. Its main goal is to develop technical capabilities in entrepreneurship and business and to foster entrepreneurial mindsets through the practical implementation of these concepts.

Neak Oknha Dr. Pung Kheav Se serves as Chairman of Canadia Bank and Overseas Cambodian Investment Corporation and is actively involved in the investment and development activities of both companies. A distinguished entrepreneur and respected business leader in Cambodia and Canada, Neak Oknha Dr. Pung Kheav Se has served as Chairman, President, CEO and Board Member of several companies, including Oriental Ship Supplies, Oriental Commercial Inc, and has led Canadia Bank’s growth since 1991. He used to be a Chairman of the Association of Banks in Cambodia and also serves as President of the Cambodia Constructors Association, working closely with industry leaders to guide the development of the banking and construction sectors in Cambodia.
Among the honors and awards Neak Oknha Dr. Pung Kheav Se holds a Mahaserey Vattanac Award presented by His Majesty, Norodom Sihanouk, King-Father of Cambodia in 2002; and “The Highest National Contribution” medal awarded by Prime Minister Hun Sen, presented by His Majesty, Norodom Sihamoni King of Cambodia in 2012, for the significant contributions he has made and continues to make toward the development of Cambodia.
On November 21st, 2019, Neak Oknha Dr. Pung Kheav Se was honorary as Doctor of Business Administration under representative of by Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo HUN SEN, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Cambodia during the inauguration of the Indradevi Building of the Royal Academy of Cambodia.

On November 30, 2021, from 5:30 to 7:00 pm, undergraduate students of the University of Technology and Science of Cambodia (CamTech) led by Mr. Mut Somoeun, an expert in “Khmer Culture and History” visited the Bokator Khmeng Wat Than Club, branch II located in Borey Sony, Sangkat Steung Meanchey, Khan Meanchey, Phnom Penh. The purpose of this study visit is to deepen the understanding of a lesson on Khmer traditional martial arts in the subject “Khmer Studies and Introduction to History” as well as to see the greatness of Khmer traditional martial arts “Bokator”.

In an interview with us, Mr. Athan Sena Sdech Hanuman, who is the instructor there, said that Khmer Bokator was created by Khmer people a long time ago. The instructor added that the word “Bokator” is sometimes called “Labokator”. According to Samdech Chuon Nath’s dictionary “Labokator” means a short stick to hold the forearm as a protection against a long stick, but these two terms do not seem to be in common use today. Not only did our team get the opportunity to gain a better understanding of the history, meaning, characteristics, and benefits of practicing and using Khmer traditional martial arts “Bokator”, we also got to see the performance of Bokator, and our students got to participate in practical Bokator practice in a pleasant atmosphere.

This is the key message from Athan Sena Sdech Hanuman to Cambodian people, especially the youth, “Please support the traditional Khmer martial art “Bokator” and join training together for physical and mental health, self-defense, and national defense as well as preservation of this martial art.”

Camtech University would like to thank Mr. Athan, the Founder and General Manager of Bokator Khmeng Wat Than Club, for allowing us to have a study visit at his club. This visit really provided our students with hands-on experience in seeing with their own eyes and practicing what they have studied in class. We would also like to support and participate in preserving this precious heritage of ancient Khmer martial arts.

## Center For Socio-Economic Research

The Center for Socio-Economic Research (CSER) is CamTech’s research institute dedicated to social and economic development of Cambodia and beyond.

CSER pioneers research studies, generates new academic knowledge, and integrates quantitative and qualitative methods across the fields in social science to advance our understanding on social phenomena and promote welfare. On top of that, we work to coordinate and support local and regional researchers, faculty members, students, and social scientists to bring new ideas into the world through research development and skills training program and seminars. • Human capital development

• Social development program and impact evaluation

• Demographic analysis and population development

• Migration and remittances

• Labor, employment, and wage

• Agriculture, rural development, and poverty reduction

• Science, technology, and socio-economic development

• Small and Medium sized Enterprise (SME) development

## Comparative Education Society Of Cambodia

## Comparative Education Society Of Cambodia

Comparative Education Society of Cambodia (CESCam) was established in 2018 by a group of prominent researchers in the field of educational research, but it was not until 2021 that CESCam’s permanent secretariat has been established at CamTech as a focal point for communication and logistics following a board of director’s meeting. Currently, CamTech’s president Dr. Khieng Sothy is also the elected-president of CESCam.

Overall vision of CESCam is to promote comparative education in Cambodia through fostering teaching and research in the area of comparative education, producing publication about Cambodian education and beyond, contributing to advancing philosophy, methodology and methods, and establishing networks with local and international research and educational institutions and other counterpart societies.

CamTech shares a similar vision as CESCam, and the former intends to stimulate intellectual environment and contribute with out-of-the-box thinking and detail-oriented research studies to address key issues in the Cambodian educational system. Our areas of research include:

- Economics of education
- Innovative and emerging models of education
- Digital education
- STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics) education
- Research culture and practice in higher education institutions
- Internationalization of higher education
- University-Industry partnership

# History

## History

# History

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education.

The idea of a university was the brainchild of **Neak Oknha Dr Pung Kheav Se** in 2018 to enable young talents to receive a high level of tertiary education. The university was named the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) and receives support from the Federation of Khmer-Chinese in Cambodia with an *aim to cultivate Cambodian young professional talents in science and technology and enhance Cambodia’s economic development*, with technical partnership with established and reputable universities in the Asian region. In return, CamTech will equip their students with academic and hands-on training, which will increase their employability and contribute to the development of Cambodia.

*During the meeting  with  the Founder and the  Representative  of  Tianjin University of Technology, HE Dr* *Hang Chuon Naron**, the* *Minister of Education, Youth and Sport**, expressed his full support to the project of CamTech University.*

In March 2021, **CamTech** received the official approval from the Royal Government of Cambodia to operate with the establishment of five faculties: the Faculty of Engineering, the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, the Faculty of Business and Management, the Faculty of Applied Sciences, and the Faculty of Sustainable Built Environment. 

**Not-profit Status**The University is a private not-for-profit institution with the mission of enabling young bright students from different backgrounds to be equipped with quality education and practical skills to contribute to the development of Cambodia. The University can pursue income-generating activities, as long as any surplus is reinvested back into the University, to ensure quality and sustainability.

**Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Se Foundation**To contribute to the establishment of the university, Neak Oknha Pung Kheav Foundation (the Foundation) was founded. The Foundation has provided 5 hectares of land in Chroy Changva Satellite city as the campus of the CamTech University, and invested more than $3 million to build the campus with the main university building, state-of-the-art facilities, a garden and a canteen.

# Industry Linkage

The University-Industry Linkage (UIL) in CamTech was established with the aim to enhance knowledge and technology transfer for students by exposing them to the real-world industries.   - Build new networks and collaborations with local and international companies and organizations
  - Maintain good relationships with existing industry/firm partners
  - Attract start-ups or companies to locate their bases within the university campus

The School of Continuing Education (SCE) aims to empower lifelong learners and creates a lifelong learning society in Cambodia.

We design training courses and programs that focus on practical applications, workplace relevance, and development of forward-thinking ability to thrive in future uncertainty. On top of that, the School of Continuing Education functions as a school within CamTech providing short-term skills training and professional development programs to grow individuals’ knowledge and proficiency with university-level education but without the time and cost commitment of a full degree. We also work closely with both public and private sectors to design on-trend and competency-based curricula that equip you with marketable qualification and expertise to meet current demand for skills and give you the competitive edge at workplace.

The 21st century is characterized by rapid change in science and technology, but with it, come the necessity to frequently adjust to the prerequisite of knowledge otherwise individual current set of skills will be deemed obsolete in a fairly short period. To CamTech, there is no such notion as finished education, but we also believe that adult education per se should not be limited only to formal academic degree. In addition, each individual has different pace of learning and attention interval. For this reason, individuals should be allowed for flexibility in their own appropriate learning styles.

The School of Graduate Studies (SGS) at CamTech University has a philosophy deeply rooted in a proactive response to the dynamic challenges facing our world today, particularly in the context of Industry Revolution 4.0 and its environmental and social implications. Positioned strategically, SGS aims to address these complexities through its overarching theme: “Science, Technology, and Sustainability (STS).” At the heart of SGS’s philosophy are three foundational pillars: academic excellence, impacts on career, and community engagement. These pillars serve as guiding principles shaping the core curriculum across all majors, embodying a holistic approach to graduate education. The vision of becoming a leading graduate school in STS is intricately woven into the design of the core curriculum, aligning educational objectives with the broader goal of producing skilled graduates capable of addressing complex issues in sustainable development. The goals and objectives further solidify this philosophy, emphasizing the establishment of SGS as a center for interdisciplinary collaboration and engagement. By offering high-quality master’s and doctoral programs, fostering diverse perspectives, and prioritizing critical thinking and problem-solving skills, the core curriculum reflects a commitment to nurturing well-rounded individuals poised to make significant contributions in their respective fields.

# Media and Communication Technology Program Overview

December 6, 2023 2024-11-07 10:38
## Program Overview

A Bachelor’s degree in Media and Communication Technology is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on various aspects of media technology, including digital media production, telecommunications, multimedia systems, and network engineering. It combines the study of communication theories, media production, digital technologies, and business management. The overall purpose of this program is to equip students with necessary knowledge and skills to succeed in the rapid growth of media and communication technology in order to prepare them for careers in media and communication companies or self-employment as independent media producers. Throughout the 4-year program, students will learn about the emerging technologies, history and theory of media and communication. The program will provide practical aspects of producing various media forms such as audio, video, and web content. Students will gain an understanding of digital technologies and their impact on communication practices and media industries. In addition, students will have opportunities to complete internships or other practical experiences to gain hands-on experience in the field at the industry or virtually.

## Program Learning Outcomes

- Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the principles, theories, and practices of media and communication technology.

- Apply practical knowledge and skills of various hardware and software tools to design, create, and produce digital content.

- Communicate effectively through different mediums of communication, including writing, speaking, and visual media.

- Critically analyze situations, identify problems, and develop solutions using creative and innovative approaches.

- Work collaboratively with others from diverse backgrounds, and aware of ethical issues related to media and communication technologies and demonstrate professionalism.

- Adapt to changes in technology and media landscapes and continue to learn and update new skills throughout the career pathway.

## Program Structure

The 4-year Bachelor’s Degree program contains 156 credits combining from 106 credits of coursework, 48 credits of internship and 2 credits of Industrial Placement Report. The courses are divided into three categories, including Common Courses, Specialized Courses, and Elective Courses.

One of the video series of “Message from President” In this video, Dr. Sothy Khieng, president of CamTech, highlighted how important STEM education is for the future of Cambodia and its people. STEM, an acronym that refers to science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, mainly is a field of study and a career path related to industry 4.0, digitalization, and the use of information technology. From his extensive experience across the globe from the USA, Europe, and Asia, Dr. Sothy Khieng concluded that to maintain a prosperous future for Cambodia and its economic growth, Cambodia’s younger generation needs to shift from low-skill careers to technology-oriented careers, in short, STEM careers. A publication in 2016 by Saint Blanquat & Associates, Co., Ltd. funded by the British Embassy in Phnom Penh lists the top 20 careers in Cambodia over the next 10 years, which include production line supervisors, automation technicians, architects, civil engineers, construction site supervisors, health and safety engineers, construction project managers, water supply experts, water sanitation experts, quality assurance specialists, chemists, public health analysts, doctors (general practitioners), medical laboratory technicians, psychologists, economists, actuaries, financial analysts, mechanics, network analysts, and software programmers.

Dr. Khieng Sothy, representing CamTech University, signed a Tri-Party MOU with Smart Axiata, represented by Mr. Feiruz Ikhwan, acting CEO of Smart Axiata, and Impact Hub Phnom Penh (Cambodia) Co. Ltd., represented by Mrs. Melanie Mossard, CEO of Impact Hub Phnom Penh, regarding an online entrepreneur platform using the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform Program. The signing event had honorable presents from H.E. Dr. Hang Chuon Narong, Minister of Education, and H.E. Vandeth Chea, Minister of Post and Telecommunications. CamTech is a private, non-profit, and research-incentive university among ten leading public and private universities that signed this MOU. Two of our senior lecturers had completed entrepreneurship training using the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform prior to this event. CamTech will use the SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform as part of entrepreneurship courses as well as in our Social Innovation Center (SCI).

The SmartStart Unipreneur Learning Platform is an educational initiative between Impact Hub Phnom Penh and Smart Axiata Co., Ltd. It is the first local online learning platform that introduces entrepreneurship through a blended learning approach to Cambodian students in Khmer and English. Its main goal is to develop technical capabilities in entrepreneurship and business and to foster entrepreneurial mindsets through the practical implementation of these concepts.

Member

**Mr Kang Leng**

**CEO, ISI GROUP**

Cambodian born Kang Leng, CEO of ISI GROUP, spent a decade gaining international exposure, experience and education in Singapore and Australia. Leng first studied Bachelor of Commerce (Accounting and Marketing) and went on to complete a Master of Commerce (in Organizational Management) both at the University of New South Wales. Afterwards he worked as a Capital Gain Tax Accountant in States Street, Sydney, for two years.

Returned to Cambodia in 2009 with a passion for entrepreneurship that creates positive impacts and contributions to society, Leng first joined ISI GROUP as an assistant to the Founder. He became Managing Director of ISI STEEL, the founding company of ISI GROUP, in 2011 after having successfully transformed various functions such as the Operations, Accounting & Finance, Procurement, Sales and Marketing. He then became CEO of ISI GROUP in 2017, where he sits today.

Under Leng’s leadership, ISI GROUP has transformed from a small, family-run business into a successful and respectable mid-size corporation with clear vision, core values, good corporate governance and organizational structure. Leng has led ISI GROUP into a number of related diversifications such building material distribution, pre-engineering steel building solution, property development as well as investment into technology start-ups and Cambodia’s iconic F&B brand, Brown Coffee and Bakery to capture the opportunities in the growing economy of Cambodia. He is dedicated to creating positive changes through the work of ISI GROUP and related CSR programs through KMH Foundation. In recognition of Leng’s contribution, he was awarded Distinguished Private Entrepreneurship Award in 2021 by YEAC, and Outstanding Donor Support in Education Award in 2022 by EdTech Asia.

Mr. Moniroth Thou holds a Bachelor of Fine and Applied Arts in Industrial Design from the School of Architecture and Design at King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi (KMUTT). With a strong passion for innovation and a business-driven mindset, Mr. Moniroth applies his expertise in design and research to transform ideas into practical opportunities. At CamTech University, he contributes to the university’s growth by supporting the development of strategic campaigns and initiatives that enhance institutional visibility and engagement. He is detail-oriented, continuously pushes boundaries, and believes that “luck is hackable.”

Visiting Professor of Entrepreneurship

Visiting Professor of Entrepreneurship

An ASEAN-focused Serial Entrepreneur, Mr. Stephen Lai is a former multinational executive who has spent over 30 years accumulating cross-cultural business experience and extensive global people networks while overseeing offices in Singapore (HQ), Hong Kong, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Saigon and Mumbai, and pioneering large scale commodity and investment conferences in ten major cities across Asia. An EXCO member of the ASEAN Economic Club and Business Adviser to KSI. Strategic Institute for Asia Pacific, Stephen is currently Chairman of Malaysia-China (Greater Bay Area) Science-Tech Innovation Alliance and Founder-President of Penang-Chengdu Friendship Association. During 2012-2014, he was tasked to promote internationalization of China enterprises under the Belt and Road Initiative when he was appointed Executive Adviser to the Director of China Council for the Promotion of International Trade Shenzhen Municipal Committee, who was concurrently President of China (Shenzhen) International Chamber of Commerce. In addition, Stephen served as Deputy Director on the China (Shenzhen) Financial Expo and Conference Planning Committee chaired by Shenzhen Mayor for 5 years. A business mentor and fund raising adviser to tech start-up CEO’s in Silicon Valley, Singapore and Penang, Stephen also actively consults with Chinese Enterprises in the areas of international business and partnership development in ASEAN countries. A former Adviser to BuonMaThuot Coffee Exchange Centre, Vietnam’s first commodity exchange, Stephen’s varied international career includes a stint as Chief Representative (ASEAN) for one of China’s largest fintech solution providers listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, Regional Business Development roles with global financial information giant Reuters, Investment Technology Manager with Koeneman Capital Management – Asia’s first quant-based boutique investment firm founded by former Head of Equities at Government Investment Corporation (GIC) of Singapore- and Business Consultant to Singapore Government’s premier ICT R&D Centre, Kent Ridge Digital Lab (later renamed A*STAR). An Industrial Adviser and Adjunct Professor at DRB-HICOM University of Automotive. Malaysia, Stephen is an Industrial Entrepreneurship Fellow at the Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM). He earned an MBA from the Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor and double degrees in Mathematics and Electrical Engineering from the University of Texas at Austin. A former ASEAN Scholar in Singapore, Penang-born Stephen is a Certified Career. Coach and enjoys training youths in the areas of Resilience and leadership. Development and Social Entrepreneurship. During 2018-2021, he served as Strategic Adviser to Penang State Minister for Trade, Industry and Entrepreneur Development in his home state in Malaysia.

Advisor (Business Development)

and Visiting Lecturer (Entrepreneurship)

Thierry joined OCIC Group as Vice President in December 2022 and has played an instrumental role in catalyzing the organization’s growth. His role encompasses a diverse range of responsibilities including business development, innovation, transformation, and sustainability. Under his leadership, the group made significant advancements in the development and evolution of Koh Pich and positioning Cambodia as an attractive destination for international investors.

Thierry has also held leadership roles as country manager and CEO at Airbus Group and Airbus Helicopters in the Philippines, as well as regional sales roles in Singapore and Hong Kong – delivering US$11 billion in revenue for the French aerospace group.

In addition to his role as VP at OCIC group, Thierry continues to wear multiple hats as an entrepreneur, investor, advisor, and board director. His entrepreneurial spirit has led him to establish 10 companies since 2012 and he has led the growth of several startups, SMEs, and publicly listed multinational companies.

One of the highlights of his career was in 2018 as CEO of Dara Ventures, a startup and joint venture with the OCIC Group that focuses on asset management and innovation.

His aviation company, PhilJets, an aviation startup launched in 2013, managed assets exceeding USD200 million. In 2017 he launched Negocia Capital, a VC funding over 20 startups focusing on tech and impact investments.

Thierry is also a successful angel investor with a diversified portfolio of companies across industry sectors including agriculture, retail, distribution and trading and real estate, to aviation, fintech and blockchain.

Thierry graduated from the Harvard Business School’s Owner & President Management Program (OPM). He also holds degrees from the Executive Management Programs at INSEAD Business School and the Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business. Thierry also holds a master’s degree in Management and International Business from INSEEC Business School in France and a bachelor’s degree in Finance and International Business from Novancia Business School in France.

As a YPO (Young President Organization) Cambodia member with an impressive track record, Thierry is a firm believer in giving back and is committed to mentoring and cultivating the next generation of leaders. He serves as an Advisor and Visiting Lecturer of Entrepreneurship at Cambodia University of Science and Technology (CamTech) and continues to shape the future by nurturing emerging leaders using his multi-sector business experience and expertise.

**Mr. Thierry Tea** 

**Vice Chairman of the Federation of Cambodian Startups** 

**Vice President of OCIC**

Thierry Tea is Vice Chairman of the Federation of Cambodian Startups and Vice President of OCIC. OCIC is part of Canadia Group, which also owns Canadia Bank Cambodia’s largest locally-owned bank. With 17,500 employees, OCIC is one of Cambodia’s largest conglomerates, investing in real estate, infrastructure, schools, hospitals, hotels, malls, and industrial parks. Its key projects include Phnom Penh’s Techo International Airport, one of the largest in Asia upon completion. Thierry was CEO of Airbus Helicopters Philippines and is the founder and Chairman of PhilJets, a private aviation and MRO company in Manila. PhilJets has created over 600 jobs and is a member of the Makati Business Club. He also serves on the Advisory Board of CamTech University and is a Harvard Business School OPM alumnus. Through his private equity firm, Negocia Capital, Thierry has invested in 20+ startups across Cambodia and the Philippines, focusing on social impact.

On Friday, January 28, Ms Song Khenglay, EVP and COO of Canadia Bank; Ms. Chheng Sophea, Head of Consumer Banking Division; Mr Sam Haung, Head of the HR Department visited, CamTech University to discuss with the CamTech’s team led by Dr. Khieng Sothy, President of CamTech University, on potential areas of collaboration between the two institutions. Canadia Bank and CamTech University had a fruitful discussion by identifying key areas of collaboration, such as internship and employment for students, short training courses and knowledge sharing sessions, joint research and consultancy projects, potential innovation projects such as those to promote cashless payment, property loan/student loan, and STEM Genius Scholarship. Canadia Bank and CamTech University shared the same vision and goals, reflecting Neak Oknha Dr. Pung Khiev Se’s commitment to promoting innovation to support the vision of Digital Economy and Society of Cambodia.

## Ms. Sovanndanny Thaverry Khuth

###### Ms. Sovanndanny Thaverry Khuth

Global Engagement Officer

Ms. Sovanndanny joined CamTech University in February 2026 as Global Engagement Officer. She has experience in international cooperation and STI policy, with previous roles at the United Nations and UNESCO.

Before joining CamTech, she interned at the United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs (UNODA) in Geneva, where she supported the humanitarian disarmament framework. Her work focused on preparing policy and briefing documents, particularly on emerging technologies and the governance of artificial intelligence in armed conflict. She contributed to multilateral negotiations under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, especially with the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, and helped coordinate high-level meetings for Protocol II, Protocol V, the Arms Trade Treaty, the Convention on Cluster Munitions, and the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

She also worked as a Consultant in the Science, Technology, and Innovation Policy Section at UNESCO in Paris, following a six-month traineeship. She contributed to the 2021 UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science and helped organize international events on science diplomacy, gender equality in science, and open science monitoring.

Sovanndanny holds a dual master’s degree in Applied International Law and International Politics from Université de Sherbrooke and graduated Magna Cum Laude in International Affairs from Sciences Po Bordeaux. Her research examines disinformation in the Sahel, focusing on narrative patterns and their impact on geopolitical perceptions in unstable political environments.

Ms. Khan Kuntheary earned a Master’s degree in Business Administration, specializing in Finance from National University of Management. Ms. Kuntheary has 18-year working experience in the field of accounting and finance and made great contributions to several big local and foreign-owned companies. She was an accounting manager at CIA First International School for more than 10 years, and she then moved to a new company, Ramatex Group, where she worked as an accounting manager for 2 years. Ms. Kuntheary rapidly advanced to a top position in the field of finance, holding a position as finance manager of GM Property. Ms. Kuntheary’s fast advancement in her career is attributed to her strong technical skills in accounting and finance, some of which include Quick Book, Peachtree, ERP, Conical-hate, UBS system, advanced Excel, financial analysis and reporting, Cambodian taxation. In addition, Ms. Kuntheary possesses strong management skills in coaching and training, KPI management, team management.

Visiting Professor

Asst. Prof. Pradorn Sureephong, Ph.D. received his double degree in Informatique from Universite Lumiere Lyon 2, France and in Knowledge Management from Chiang Mai University, Thailand. He is the associate director in innovation and joint ventures and also head of master degree program in Digital Technology Management at College of Arts, Media and Technology. He is also the president of the Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering Association (ECTI – North Section). He secured multiple research grants from British Council (2012), French Embassy – PHC SIAM (2015), Horizon H2020 by European Commission (2017). He is now the local coordinator of 3 Erasmus+ programme i.e. SUNSpACe (Sustainable Development Smart Agriculture Capacity, CENTRAL (Digital Transformation Capacity Building), DigiHealth (Digital Health and Monitoring). He is also one of the leaders in AgriTech startup and Young Smart Farmer incubation in Thailand. He in training 500+ Young Smart Farmers in northern Thailand under the New Genetic Graduate program funded by Ministry of Higher Education, Sciences and Innovation. He had 12 successful PhD completions under his direct supervision. He has published more than 100 articles in national and international journal. He is top 5 researcher in field of digital innovation at Chiang Mai University.

---

Research Fellow

Dr. RET Thearom obtained a Ph.D. in social psychology, specializing in the social psychology of work and organizations, from the Aix-Marseille University (AMU), France. He also has a Master’s degree in Developmental Psychology from the University of Toulouse II-Le Mirail, France, and a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology from the Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP), Cambodia. Dr. Ret has been a faculty member teaching and conducting research at the department of psychology of RUPP since 2011. In addition, he currently teaches BA, MA, and Ph.D. students in psychology, social work, leadership, and educational research in the field of social and behavioral sciences at various higher education institutions. Dr. RET has more than ten years of experience teaching, coaching, supervision, research, and psychological treatment for NGOs and private and public institutions. His research interests and areas of expertise involve mainly mental health issues in the workplace, problems of learning and teaching in school settings, evidence-based approaches in psychotherapy, Applied Social Psychology and Neuroscience for leadership, diplomacy, and community healing.

---

Dr Tineke WATER is a Public Health Consultant with the World Bank Cambodia and Academic Advisor for Future Forum, an independent policy think tank for young researchers, and visiting Professor of Public Health at the Cambodian University of Technology, Phnom Penh, Cambodia. She holds a PhD (child health) from AUT University, New Zealand, and a MA in Development Studies (with a focus on Global Health) from the University of Auckland, New Zealand.

Tineke’s research expertise and focus is on social science and participatory research with children/youth, public health, humanitarian response and disaster/emergency response (HIV, nutrition, diarrheic disease) and health care ethics. She continues to work with organization’s/universities to support research and postgraduate study; and consults for international NGOs related to child/maternal/public health; in addition to continuing to publish in international journals.

---

Mr. Vladimir Lazarov has lived in Europe, Africa, and Australia but calls Cambodia his home country. He has more than 11 years of experience teaching English to local university and high school students. Mr. Vladimir Lazarov strongly believes that understanding the Khmer culture and values is an important aspect of providing effective education. He is driven by passion and desire to make a difference. Teaching is a very rewarding career that gives a sense of fulfillment where the learning process extends beyond the limits of a textbook or geographical borders. Knowledge is boundless, and by teaching others, we learn more and eventually become better human beings.

Visiting Research Fellow

Prof. Wang was the founding Head of Department of Mechatronics and Robotics. He is an IET Fellow and a senior member of IEEE. He is also a team leader of Talented Jiangsu Innovation and Entrepreneur Programme. He has broad academic working experience in China, England, Wales, and Scotland for more than 20 years. He has extensive research experience in Internet of Things (IoT), wireless mesh networks, indoor positioning, big data analytics, and applications for smart cities. Along with more 30 research projects sponsored from EU, UK EPSRC, Innovate UK, China NSFC, and industry, his research in each area has led to an impactful industrial product. For example, the smart trolley, which has been deployed at more than 10 airports in China, he has developed with industrial partner is the first in the world to provide an IoT solution aiming at providing intelligent airport services for passengers. His collaborative research in acoustic localisation with Zhejiang University has won the first place in Microsoft Indoor Localisation Competition in sound group. He has nearly 200 publications and filed dozens of patents, including 15 granted patents in the US, Japan, South Korea, and China. His research has been classified as World Leading at the UK’s REF assessment. The highest citation number of a single technical paper is nearly 600.

His current research interests include intelligent manufacturing and healthcare. In intelligent manufacturing, he is investigating a system dubbed as VisionTwin to integrate industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), edge computing, machine vision, digital twin, and artificial intelligence to promote the intelligence of manufacturing. One application example is condition monitoring of overhead power lines, where a 3-dimensional space could be created on a typical 2-D camera. Apart from power system, he is investigating technologies for robots, particularly on Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). In healthcare, he has led a team to develop a novel application of diagnosing COVID-19 on smartphones by monitoring users’ breathing. In addition, he is investigating technologies for motion and posture detection of users indoors by acoustic analysis on smartphones. He is currently organizing two international conferences, HCCS and CollaborateCom. If you would like to collaborate with me on research or study with me for a PhD degree, feel free to contact me.

The Professional Diploma Programs at Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) is designed for career focused, accomplished an associate degree or the equivalent. Students enrolled in the Professional Diploma will elevate their focus-expertise to a professional level and learn critical skills in entrepreneurship, freelancing work, and other business-related skills. PDP provides a pass way to full bachelor’s program after students complete the program and fulfill the requirements for chosen major.

Students enrolled in this program will identify a focus area that complements their major area studies and supports the development of their professional goals. This program gives students the opportunity to deepen and expand their readiness to enter and be leaders within an ever-changing specialties by broadening their skill sets and access to a variety of techniques ready for work. Their coursework will prepare them to engage in repertoire planning that demands more diversity in programming, addressing current needs and gaps in the professional world. The program includes a career-focused seminar, core coursework and student-selected job placement-learning, in addition to private lessons, large ensembles, electives courses.

កិច្ចសហប្រតិបត្តិការត្រីភាគី (Triple helix) គឺជាវាក្យស័ព្ទដែលគេប្រើជាទូទៅសំដៅទៅលើអន្តរកម្មរវាងអ្នកចូលរួមចំណែកបីស្ថាប័នផ្សេងគ្នា រួមមាន អ្នកសិក្សាឧស្សាហកម្ម និងរដ្ឋាភិបាល។ ប៉ុន្តែ គេក៏អាចបន្ថែម ពាក្យ “សហគមន៍” ចូលទៅក្នុងនៅក្នុងគំរូកិច្ចសហប្រតិបត្តិការត្រីភាគីនេះអោយក្លាយជាគំរូ កិច្ចសហប្រតិបត្តិការចតុភាគី (Quadruple helix)។ កត្តាទាំងបួននៅក្នុងគំរូខាងលើនេះ អាចមានអន្តរកម្មជាមួយគ្នា និងអាចច្របាប់បញ្ចូលគ្នាដើម្បីបង្កើតជាផលប្រយោជន៍អោយគ្នាទៅវិញទៅមក ក៏ដូចជាមានប្រយោជន៍ដល់សង្គមទាំងមូល។ទាំងនេះគឺជាខ្លឹមសារគោលនៃ កម្មវិធីបណ្តុះបណ្តាលសមត្ថភាព វគ្គទី៧ របស់ សាកលវិទ្យាល័យខេមតិចដែលបានធ្វើឡើងនៅថ្ងៃសៅរ៍ ទី២៧ ខែវិច្ឆិកា ឆ្នាំ២០២១ កន្លងទៅ ដោយ សាស្រ្តាចារ្យ បណ្ឌិត Shahir Liew មកពីសាកលវិទ្យាល័យបច្ចេកវិទ្យា PETRONAS (Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS)។ សាកលវិទ្យាល័យខេមតិចគឺជាសាកលវិទ្យាល័យដែលផ្តោតលើ បច្ចេកទេសនិងបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ហើយសាកលវិទ្យាល័យខេមតិច នឹងប្រើប្រាស់គំរូកិច្ចសហប្រតិបត្តិការចតុភាគីនេះដើម្បីចូលរួមចំណែកក្នុងការអភិវឌ្ឍន៍ កំលាំងពលកម្មរបស់ប្រទេសកម្ពុជាដើម្បីជំរុញអោយមានការអភិវឌ្ឍន៍ប្រទេសទាំងមូល។ នៅសាកលវិទ្យាល័យខេមតិចពួកយើងផ្តោតលើការរៀនឥតឈប់ ការបន្តការលើកកំពស់សមត្ថភាព និងការធ្វើការងារជាក់ស្តែង។

The triple helix is a common term used to refer to the interaction among three main stakeholders: “academia, industry, and government”. However, “community” should and can be thrown into this model to make the “quadruple helix” model. These four actors in the model can interact and merge to produce various mutual benefits as well as benefits for the whole society in general. This is the key message from CamTech Professional Development session 7, conducted on Saturday 27th November 2021 by Professor Shahir Liew, Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS. As a science and technology university, CamTech will use the quadruple helix concept to contribute to the development of the Cambodian workforce to propel development for the whole nation. At CamTech, we keep on learning, improving, and doing practical work.

This is the key message from CamTech Professional Development session 7, conducted on Saturday 27th November 2021 by Professor Shahir Liew, Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS. As a science and technology university, CamTech will use the quadruple helix concept to contribute to the development of the Cambodian workforce to propel development for the whole nation. At CamTech, we keep on learning, improving, and doing practical work.

CamTech cares about professional development of our faculty members and staff and thus provides regular training sessions. On Saturday 11th December 2021, CamTech had great honor that Prof. Heidi Dahles of Griffith University and University Tasmania gave us a talk on “Writing for Publication”. For young researchers, it is necessary to understand what should be done in order to get their research papers published, especially in high impact journals. There were some key messages that the presentation conveyed. First, a good researcher must be also a good reader. Reading will provide researchers with ideas to write about. Second, your research should contribute to the existing knowledge, and thus it should propose to fill a gap or gaps in the literature. Third, a good researcher is also a good collaborator. Research is a tiring job and time consuming, so a researcher should find a partner or partners to share responsibility. Another benefit from collaboration is the contribution from experts from different fields, which are very beneficial for producing a well-rounded research work for publication. These three messages aforementioned are only examples of good practices for writing for publication, while in fact, there are many other factors to consider when one takes up a research project and aim to write for publication. Learning from peers and one’s own experience is vitally important for personal growth in any areas, including research and writing for publication.

🔹 Confucian-Buddhist Synergy: Combine “rén” (benevolence) and mindfulness to prioritize collective well-being over profit-driven systems.

The study combines theoretical concepts with practical applications in order to prepare students to analyse data and make informed decisions that mitigate business risks and improve organizational performance.

Students learn to develop risk management strategies, assess potential threats to businesses, evaluate financial risks, and analyse market trends. They also gain skills in data mining, statistical analysis, decision-making, database management, and software development. The program covers topics such as business intelligence, strategic management, enterprise risk management, fraud detection and prevention, cyber security, and compliance. Graduates can pursue careers in various industries, including finance, insurance, healthcare, government, and consulting firms.

Overall, a Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management and Business Intelligence provides students with a strong foundation in both technical and business skills, making them well-equipped to succeed in today’s data-driven business world.

## Program Learning Outcomes

At the end of the 4-year program, graduates will be able to:

- Use quantitative and qualitative tools to assess risk and identify potential threats to businesses and organizations.
- Develop and implement comprehensive risk management plans to minimize losses and protect the interests of their companies and clients.
- Apply critical thinking and analytical skills to business intelligence data and use it to recommend data-driven strategies to help organizations remain competitive.
- Demonstrate knowledge of information security principles to protect data privacy and prevent data breaches.
- Effectively communicate complex risk management, business intelligence, and compliance issues to stakeholders, including senior executives, regulators, employees, and clients.

## Program Structure

The 4-year Bachelor’s Degree program contains 156 credits combining from 106 credits of coursework, 48 credits of internship and 2 credits of Industrial Placement Report. The courses are divided into three categories, including Common Courses, Specialized Courses, and Elective Courses.

# Robotics and Automation Engineering Program Overview

December 6, 2023 2025-11-17 14:40
## Program Overview

Robotics and Automation Engineering prepares students to eaxcel in the rapidly-evolving world of industrial 4.0 and digital transformation for industrial manufacturing. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the practical skills they need to succeed in this exciting and dynamic demanding field. It focuses on building a strong foundation of engineering principles, computer science, mechanical design, and new technology for industrial digital transformation. The unique features of the Robotics and Automation Engineering program at Camtech is its project-based learning program in which students work on internship projects for 3 years to adapt new technologies quickly and to develop excellent problem-solving and collaborative teamwork skills from their early years In addition to the hand-on approach in the university, the one-year industry placement program will provide students with an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a real-world work environment, helping them acquire practical knowledge and skills that can prepare them for a successful career. As graduates of this program, students will be well-equipped to design, develop, and implement robotic systems and automation technology that can improve efficiency and productivity across a range of industries.

## Program Learning Outcomes

- Acquire an extensive comprehension of robotics and automation, encompassing the past developments in robotics, existing software and hardware technologies, and anticipated future advancements. (knowledge)
- Understand and apply principles of robotics mechanics and control, including kinematics, dynamics, and control algorithms (Cognitive Skills)
- Develop critical thinking and problem-solving abilities to construct robots by utilizing various fabrication technologies like 3D printing, CNC machining, and others and additionally, acquire proficiency in programming robots, including motion planning, path optimization, and control algorithms(Cognitive Skills)
- Apply ethical considerations in the development of robots, automation, and intelligent systems, including issues related to bias, privacy, and data security (Interpersonal Skill and Responsibility)
- Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements and trends in the field of robotic and automation including both software and hardware (Interpersonal Skill and Responsibility)
- Develop effective team work and communication skills to present complex industry automation scenario to both technical and non-technical audiences (Communication, Psychomotor Skills)

The School of Continuing Education (SCE) aims to empower lifelong learners and creates a lifelong learning society in Cambodia.

We design training courses and programs that focus on practical applications, workplace relevance, and development of forward-thinking ability to thrive in future uncertainty. On top of that, the School of Continuing Education functions as a school within CamTech providing short-term skills training and professional development programs to grow individuals’ knowledge and proficiency with university-level education but without the time and cost commitment of a full degree. We also work closely with both public and private sectors to design on-trend and competency-based curricula that equip you with marketable qualification and expertise to meet current demand for skills and give you the competitive edge at workplace.

The 21st century is characterized by rapid change in science and technology, but with it, come the necessity to frequently adjust to the prerequisite of knowledge otherwise individual current set of skills will be deemed obsolete in a fairly short period. To CamTech, there is no such notion as finished education, but we also believe that adult education per se should not be limited only to formal academic degree. In addition, each individual has different pace of learning and attention interval. For this reason, individuals should be allowed for flexibility in their own appropriate learning styles.

The conference aims to bring together researchers and experts in Knowledge Management, Software Engineering, and Information Systems to share their ideas, experiences, and insights. We welcome researchers and practitioners from academia, industries, research institutions, R&D enterprise services and governmental organizations to exchange innovative contributions around the conference topics. This conference series was started in an international collaboration context between research professionals in Western and Asian countries in Chiang Mai, Thailand 2006. Subsequently, the next SKIMA conferences were organized in Kathmandu, Nepal in 2008; Fez, Morocco in 2009; Paro, Bhutan in 2010; Benevento, Italy in 2011, Chengdu, China in 2012, Chiang Mai Thailand in 2013, Dhaka, Bangladesh in 2014, Kathmandu Nepal in 2015, Chengdu China 2016, Colombo Sri Lanka in 2017, Phnom Penh, Cambodia in 2018 and Maldives 2019.

The workshop aims to promote the concept of Digital Sustainability, which is defined as the effort to develop and apply intelligent technologies to achieve sustainable economic growth in the context of the United Nations (UNs) SDGs. It will be a day-long workshop with the heads of national and international higher education institutions (HEIs) to share experiences about the potential and challenges of the digital transformation for institutional digital services (finance, HR, library, sports, learning management systems, etc.), e-learning, blended learning, m-learning, VR/game-based learning, etc. The workshop’s topic includes transforming cross-faculty research and innovation using new digital technologies, particularly data science and AI. It also aims to bring a new dimension to the universities to work with UNs SDG team, government agencies and policy makers to build a digital framework for a sustainable socio-economic grow.

In addition, the SKIMA family is honoured to have speakers like Prof Jeffrey Sachs, President SDSN (UN) and HE Prof Chhem K Rethy Miniter attached to the Prime Minister and State Secretary, Cambodia.

SKIMA mainly focuses on new software and information technologies. We had some excellent keynote speakers who voluntarily delivered speeches on new technology areas, including AI, big data, immersive technology, digital health and smart agriculture areas.

After at least a double-blind review, we consider 60 papers for the conference for SKIMA 22. Of 60, Cambodia had 14 accepted papers, to which CamTech Contributed eight research papers.

# Software Engineering Program Overview

December 6, 2023 2024-11-07 16:43
## Software Engineering Program Overview

## Program Overview

This software engineering major aims to prepare students for a career in software engineering by teaching them the complete process and methodologies for software engineering including business requirement elicitation, software architecture design and analysis, software development, software testing, and project management. The curriculum is designed to provide lifelong learning covering essential knowledge for algorithm and problem solving and system design and analysis. Using project-based learning, students will gain industry-level experience in the early years of the program through collaborative teamwork and the use of the latest industry tools and technologies. This hands-on approach helps students to develop essential skills such as communication, problem-solving, and teamwork that are essential in the workplace. In addition to the hand-on approach in the university, the one-year industry placement program will provide students with an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a real-world work environment, helping them acquire practical knowledge and skills that can prepare them for a successful career. Graduates of this program will have the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue various software engineering roles, including but not limited to, software developer, full-stack developer, front-end or back-end developer, DevOps engineer, software architect, database administrator, quality assurance, and more. Potential employment opportunities are diverse, ranging from healthcare and finance to technology and government sectors.

## Program Learning Outcomes

- Learn foundation knowledge of industry tools/technologies and software engineering principle and practice (knowledge)
- Analyze business requirement as well as tools and technologies used to solve real-case project effectively (Cognitive Skills)
- Apply Software Engineering principle and practice to develop high quality software application (Cognitive Skills)
- Develop software applications using suitable tools and technologies to solve a given problem (Cognitive Skill, Information Technology, and Numerical Skills)
- Learn and adapt to new technologies that emerge in the rapidly changing field of software engineering with professional ethic (Interpersonal Skill and Responsibility)
- Apply project management process and methodology to ensure effective teamwork and communication (Communication, Psychomotor Skills)

## Program Structure

The 4-year Bachelor’s Degree program contains 156 credits combining from 106 credits of coursework, 48 credits of internship and 2 credits of Industrial Placement Report. The courses are divided into three categories, including Common Courses, Specialized Courses, and Elective Courses.

Dr. Khieng is the founding President of Cambodia University of Technology and Science and advises the National Council of Science, Technology and Innovation. He served as the Vice President (Research and Administration) at Kirirom Institute of Technology between 2019-2021. He is an experienced and accomplished scholars, educator and higher education administrator. Before joining KIT, he spent ten years at Cambodia’s leading researching think-rank, Cambodia Development Resource Institute (CDRI). 

At CDRI, he co-founded and was the Head of Education Unit from 2014-2018 where he was a co-editor of Book on Cambodia Education 2015: Employment and Empowerment. He is also the author of a book on “The dawn of social enterprise in Cambodia?” which was published because of his doctoral research. 

His inter-disciplinary field of research interest includes post-secondary education, social entrepreneurship and innovation, and science and technology. He has held several research fellowship appointments, including at Griffith University, and University of Melbourne (Australia), and Swiss Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (Switzerland). Dr Khieng publishes peer-reviewed articles in various international journals. He co-founded the Comparative Education Society of Cambodia and is currently serving as a board member in this society and as an international advisory board member in Compare: A Journal of Comparative and International Education (UK). He has a PhD in Organization Sciences from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Netherlands and an MA in International Development Studies from Ohio University, USA, under the Fulbright Scholar Program during which he was the President of Ohio University Fulbright Association between 2007-2008.

The university combines academic rigor with real-world impact, preparing you not only for a career but for a meaningful life. The world is moving fast. Artificial intelligence, smart systems, robotics, energy innovation, and advanced technologies are shaping our collective future. At CamTech, we embrace these developments with curiosity, ethical responsibilities, and an interdisciplinary mindset. By joining CamTech, you are becoming part of not just a university but a dynamic and supportive community committed to innovation and positive change. I hope that your time at CamTech will provide moments for reflection and exploration, as well as academic rigor. These reflections inform CamTech’s interdisciplinary approach to education, research, and innovation. If I were to summarize CamTech in three words, they would be Job, Life, and Planet. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to cultivate graduates who can work with purpose, live with integrity, and contribute meaningfully to society and the planet. I encourage you to explore what CamTech has to offer. Visit our campus, speak with our students, and listen to their experiences. These reflections inform CamTech’s interdisciplinary approach to education, research, and innovation. If I were to summarize CamTech in three words, they would be Job, Life, and Planet. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to cultivate graduates who can work with purpose, live with integrity, and contribute meaningfully to society and the planet. I encourage you to explore what CamTech has to offer. Visit our campus, speak with our students, and listen to their experiences. Engage with our faculty and staff, whose dedication is centered on helping students flourish intellectually, ethically, and personally – in body, mind, heart, and spirit. If you are ready for transformation, our vibrant and supportive community is here to help you realize your full potential. CamTech is your platform to dream big, learn deeply, and make a difference. "

On November 30, 2021, from 5:30 to 7:00 pm, undergraduate students of the University of Technology and Science of Cambodia (CamTech) led by Mr. Mut Somoeun, an expert in “Khmer Culture and History” visited the Bokator Khmeng Wat Than Club, branch II located in Borey Sony, Sangkat Steung Meanchey, Khan Meanchey, Phnom Penh. The purpose of this study visit is to deepen the understanding of a lesson on Khmer traditional martial arts in the subject “Khmer Studies and Introduction to History” as well as to see the greatness of Khmer traditional martial arts “Bokator”.

In an interview with us, Mr. Athan Sena Sdech Hanuman, who is the instructor there, said that Khmer Bokator was created by Khmer people a long time ago. The instructor added that the word “Bokator” is sometimes called “Labokator”. According to Samdech Chuon Nath’s dictionary “Labokator” means a short stick to hold the forearm as a protection against a long stick, but these two terms do not seem to be in common use today. Not only did our team get the opportunity to gain a better understanding of the history, meaning, characteristics, and benefits of practicing and using Khmer traditional martial arts “Bokator”, we also got to see the performance of Bokator, and our students got to participate in practical Bokator practice in a pleasant atmosphere.

This is the key message from Athan Sena Sdech Hanuman to Cambodian people, especially the youth, “Please support the traditional Khmer martial art “Bokator” and join training together for physical and mental health, self-defense, and national defense as well as preservation of this martial art.”

Camtech University would like to thank Mr. Athan, the Founder and General Manager of Bokator Khmeng Wat Than Club, for allowing us to have a study visit at his club. This visit really provided our students with hands-on experience in seeing with their own eyes and practicing what they have studied in class. We would also like to support and participate in preserving this precious heritage of ancient Khmer martial arts.
